steps.title: Matching Mugs
steps.text: Maya and Jiwoo go to a small shop. The shop has *various* cups. The blue mugs are *no longer* for sale. But the green ones are on sale. Jiwoo thinks twelve thousand won is *too much* for one mug. But two mugs are twenty thousand won. They buy two *so that* they have matching mugs at work. The cashier wraps them. Now they have coffee in their green mugs every day!
steps.gloss: various 여러 가지의 · no longer 더 이상 ~ 않다 · too much 너무 많은(비싼) · so that ~하도록 · matching 똑같은, 짝이 맞는 · wrap 포장하다
questions: What color are their mugs?
Why do they buy two mugs?
steps.teach:
Reading on screen: "Matching Mugs". Text: "Maya and Jiwoo go to a small shop. The shop has various cups. The blue mugs are no longer for sale. But the green ones are on sale. Jiwoo thinks twelve thousand won is too much for one mug. But two mugs are twenty thousand won. They buy two so that they have matching mugs at work. The cashier wraps them. Now they have coffee in their green mugs every day!" Words: various 여러 가지의 · no longer 더 이상 ~ 않다 · too much 너무 많은(비싼) · so that ~하도록 · matching 똑같은, 짝이 맞는 · wrap 포장하다.
Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "What color are their mugs?" / "Why do they buy two mugs?". React to their answers; if one is not right, point to the sentence. You may add one short personal question linked to the reading. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the 'I can' check-out.

Ask the learner to pick one and show it by saying a sentence; react and praise specifically. Then end like a person: ask how this lesson felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to it, say that the next lesson is waiting for next time, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

steps.title: 아파요
steps.scene_desc: 저녁, 아파트 엘리베이터 안. 목도리를 두른 지우가 이마를 짚고, 장바구니를 든 벤이 걱정스럽게 바라봄
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "What’s wrong?" (아파요). Goal: 어디가 아픈지 말하고 걱정해 주기. Today's scene: 저녁, 아파트 엘리베이터 안. 목도리를 두른 지우가 이마를 짚고, 장바구니를 든 벤이 걱정스럽게 바라봄. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above).
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "What’s wrong?".

steps.when: 상대가 아파 보이거나 걱정될 때 물어요.
steps.extra: 대답: I don’t feel well.
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "What’s wrong?" (어디 안 좋아요?). When to use it: 상대가 아파 보이거나 걱정될 때 물어요. Note: 대답: I don’t feel well.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "I have a ___ache.".

steps.extra: I have a headache. · I have a stomachache.
steps.teach:
Expression 2 of 3: "I have a ___ache." (~가 아파요.). When to use it: 아픈 곳 + ache로 말해요. Note: I have a headache. · I have a stomachache.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "Get some rest.".

steps.when: 아픈 사람을 걱정해 줄 때 써요.
steps.extra: Get some rest. Feel better soon!
steps.teach:
Expression 3 of 3: "Get some rest." (좀 쉬어요.). When to use it: 아픈 사람을 걱정해 줄 때 써요. Note: Get some rest. Feel better soon!
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the app plays a short scene ("In the Elevator · 저녁, 엘리베이터에서") in the characters' own voices — tell them to just listen.

The app has just played this scene, "In the Elevator · 저녁, 엘리베이터에서", in the characters' own voices. The learner heard it and sees it on screen:

6. Jiwoo: "Yes, I have some at home." (네, 집에 있어요.)

frame: I have a ___ache. / I have a ___.
head: 아픈 곳
이렇게 말해요

steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: What’s wrong? / I have a ___ache. / I have a ___. Table (아픈 곳 → 이렇게 말해요):
- head 머리 → I have a headache.
- stomach 배 → I have a stomachache.
- tooth 이 → I have a toothache.
- throat 목 · back 허리 → My throat hurts. · My back hurts.
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items: 이 과의 표현: a headache · a cold · a fever

I have a *headache*. 머리가 아파요.
I have a *cold*. 감기에 걸렸어요. · I have a *fever*. 열이 나요.
head·stomach·tooth·back + *ache*

아픈 곳 + *hurts*: My back *hurts*.
여럿이면 hurt: My legs *hurt*.
걱정해 줄 때: Feel better soon!
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- 이 과의 표현: a headache · a cold · a fever: I have a headache. 머리가 아파요. / I have a cold. 감기에 걸렸어요. · I have a fever. 열이 나요. / head·stomach·tooth·back + ache
- My ___ hurts.: 아픈 곳 + hurts: My back hurts. / 여럿이면 hurt: My legs hurt. / 걱정해 줄 때: Feel better soon!
Common mistakes on screen:
- I have headache. → I have a headache. (headache는 a headache로 말해요.)
- My head is hurt. → My head hurts. (‘아파요’는 hurts.)
- I have a stomach. → I have a stomachache. (stomach는 ‘배’. 아프면 stomachache.)
- I don’t feel good well. → I don’t feel well. (well 하나로 ‘몸이 안 좋아요’.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. After that, go over each remaining mistake on screen in one short sentence (the wrong one, the right one and why), so that no mistake on screen is skipped. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.

steps.note: 예) head / headache → What’s wrong? — I have a headache. — Get some rest.
steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) head / headache → What’s wrong? — I have a headache. — Get some rest. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: head → headache | stomach → stomachache | tooth → toothache | back → backache.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to their answer, praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

This is the start of session 2 of "What’s wrong?" (아파요); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say. Start the review only after the learner has answered at least two of your small-talk questions.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "What’s wrong?" / "I have a ___ache." / "Get some rest.". One at a time: give a tiny real situation, wait for their answer and react naturally, then the next. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 아플 때: "I don’t feel well." (몸이 안 좋아요., 보통); "I have a cold." (감기에 걸렸어요., 보통); "My ___ hurts." (~가 아파요., 보통); "I have a fever." (열이 나요., 보통)
- 걱정해 주기: "Take some medicine." (약 먹어요., 보통); "Go see a doctor." (병원에 가 봐요., 보통); "Do you need anything?" (필요한 거 있어요?, 보통); "Feel better soon!" (빨리 나아요!, 친근)
- 나아졌을 때: "I’m feeling better." (좀 나아졌어요., 보통)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life and take them one per turn: say one, wait for the learner to say it and react, then the next. Then use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

Tips on screen:
- 몸: head 머리 · neck 목 · shoulder 어깨 · chest 가슴 / back 등·허리 · stomach 배 · knee 무릎 · body 몸
- 아플 때 쓰는 말: cough 기침 · temperature 체온 · tissue 휴지 / shot 주사 · injury 부상 — I injured my knee. 무릎을 다쳤어요.
Fill-in-the-blank dialogue on screen: A: What’s ___? B: I have a ___ache. (머리가 아파요.) / A: Oh no. Get some ___. Feel ___ soon! / 낱말 상자: wrong · head · rest · better
Mention each tip in one or two sentences, linked to the learner if you can. Then do the fill-in-the-blank dialogue: read it line by line, one blank per turn: stop at the blank, wait for them to fill it, and confirm. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): picture words.

Picture words on screen. New: sick (아픈), headache (두통), stomach (배), fever (열), cough (기침), medicine (약), rest (휴식), throat (목(목구멍)), back (등, 허리), shot (주사), tooth (이). Review words: doctor (의사).
Go through about six, new ones first, one word per turn: call highlight_word with the word, say it, and wait for the learner to say it before the next word. Never give several words in one turn. Now and then ask a tiny real question with the word (for example: Are you a morning person?) and react to the answer. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a word list.

Word list on screen: ill (아픈) — "I feel ill."; hurt (아프다) — "My back hurts."; head (머리) — "My head hurts."; body (몸) — "my whole body"; health (건강) — "Health is important."; weak (약한, 힘이 없는) — "I feel weak."; illness (병) — "a short illness"; cold (감기) — "I have a cold."; better (더 나은) — "I’m feeling better."; general (일반적인) — "in general 대체로"; affect (영향을 주다) — "A cold affects your sleep.".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): questions about the learner's own life.

steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "What’s wrong? (역할 카드)" (hint on screen: I have a ___. / My ___ hurts.)
- "I have a cold. What do you say?" (hint on screen: Get some rest. / Feel better soon!)
- "What do people usually do for a cold?" (hint on screen: They take some medicine. / They sleep a lot.)
- "I have a headache. Give me some advice." (hint on screen: Take some medicine. / Go see a doctor.)
- "Ask me what’s wrong." (hint on screen: What’s wrong? / Do you need anything?)
Role card on screen (the learner may answer as this role): 아픈 곳·건강 이야기는 역할 카드로만 연습해요. 실제 건강 정보는 말하지 않아요. 역할 카드: 나 — 머리가 아프고 열이 조금 있어요 (I have a headache and a fever.)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.

steps.title: Ben’s Soup
steps.text: Jiwoo has a cold. Her whole body feels weak, so she can’t go to work. At work, Chloe *takes on* Jiwoo’s tasks for a day. In the evening, Ben knocks on the door. He *has got* chicken soup and tissues. “Warm food helps,” he says. “Soup, *for instance*, is great for a cold.” The next day, Jiwoo is feeling better.
steps.gloss: weak 힘이 없는 · take on (일을) 맡다 · task 일, 업무 · have got 가지고 있다 · for instance 예를 들어 · warm 따뜻한
questions: What does Chloe do for Jiwoo?
What does Ben bring?
steps.teach:
Reading on screen: "Ben’s Soup". Text: "Jiwoo has a cold. Her whole body feels weak, so she can’t go to work. At work, Chloe takes on Jiwoo’s tasks for a day. In the evening, Ben knocks on the door. He has got chicken soup and tissues. “Warm food helps,” he says. “Soup, for instance, is great for a cold.” The next day, Jiwoo is feeling better." Words: weak 힘이 없는 · take on (일을) 맡다 · task 일, 업무 · have got 가지고 있다 · for instance 예를 들어 · warm 따뜻한.
Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "What does Chloe do for Jiwoo?" / "What does Ben bring?". React to their answers; if one is not right, point to the sentence. You may add one short personal question linked to the reading. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the 'I can' check-out.

Check-out. The 'I can' list on screen:

Ask the learner to pick one and show it by saying a sentence; react and praise specifically. Then end like a person: ask how this lesson felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to it, say that the next lesson is waiting for next time, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

steps.title: 같이 갈래요?
steps.title_en: Do you want to come with me?
steps.scene_desc: 점심시간, 회사 건물 앞. 마야가 휴대폰 화면 속 전시회 표 두 장을 보여 주며 웃고, 지우가 반갑게 고개를 끄덕임
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "Do you want to come with me?" (같이 갈래요?). Goal: 초대하고, 수락하거나 거절하기. Today's scene: 점심시간, 회사 건물 앞. 마야가 휴대폰 화면 속 전시회 표 두 장을 보여 주며 웃고, 지우가 반갑게 고개를 끄덕임. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above).
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "Do you want to ___ with me?".

steps.en: Do you want to ___ with me?
steps.extra: Do you want to see a movie with me?
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "Do you want to ___ with me?" (저랑 같이 ~할래요?). When to use it: 같이 하자고 초대해요. Note: Do you want to see a movie with me?
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "Sure, I’d love to!".

steps.extra: I’d love to = I would love to
steps.teach:
Expression 2 of 3: "Sure, I’d love to!" (그럼요, 좋아요!). When to use it: 초대에 기쁘게 대답해요. Note: I’d love to = I would love to.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "Sorry, I can’t. I’m busy.".

steps.extra: Sorry, I can’t. Maybe next time.
steps.teach:
Expression 3 of 3: "Sorry, I can’t. I’m busy." (미안해요, 못 가요. 바빠요.). When to use it: 초대를 부드럽게 거절해요. Note: Sorry, I can’t. Maybe next time.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the app plays a short scene ("Two Tickets · 점심시간, 회사 앞에서") in the characters' own voices — tell them to just listen.

steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: Do you want to ___ with me? / Sure, I’d love to! / Sorry, I can’t. I’m busy. Table (초대 → 좋을 때):
- Do you want to see a movie with me? → Sure, I’d love to!
- Would you like to come? → That sounds great.

Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.

steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- want to + 동사: Do you want to come with me? 같이 갈래요? / 더 정중하게: Would you like to come? / 대답: I’d love to! (= I would love to)
- 거절도 부드럽게: Sorry, I can’t. I’m busy. / 이유 + 다음 약속: I have other plans. Maybe next time. / 마지막에: Thanks for asking.
Common mistakes on screen:
- Do you want come with me? → Do you want to come with me? (want 뒤에 to.)
- Sure, I love to! → Sure, I’d love to! (초대에 대답할 땐 I’d love to.)
- Sorry, I can’t. I busy. → Sorry, I can’t. I’m busy. (I’m을 빼지 않아요.)
- Can I bring my friend with? → Can I bring a friend? (문장 끝에 with를 붙이지 않아요.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. After that, go over each remaining mistake on screen in one short sentence (the wrong one, the right one and why), so that no mistake on screen is skipped. Keep it light, then call next_step.

steps.note: 예) see a movie / Friday → Do you want to see a movie with me on Friday?
steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) see a movie / Friday → Do you want to see a movie with me on Friday? Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: see a movie → Friday | have lunch → tomorrow | go on a picnic → Sunday | see an opera → Saturday.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to their answer, praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

cards: Do you want to ___ with me?
steps.teach:

1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say. Start the review only after the learner has answered at least two of your small-talk questions.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "Do you want to ___ with me?" / "Sure, I’d love to!" / "Sorry, I can’t. I’m busy.". One at a time: give a tiny real situation, wait for their answer and react naturally, then the next. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

More expressions on this topic (on screen):

Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life and take them one per turn: say one, wait for the learner to say it and react, then the next. Then use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.

steps.title: Maya’s Photo Show
steps.text: Maya likes photos. A new photo book *comes out* this month, and there is a big show at the city gallery. Maya has *a couple of* tickets, so she invites Jiwoo. On Saturday morning, Jiwoo has to *deal with* some work. But she *comes back* home at noon and meets Maya at two. The photos are beautiful. After the show, they talk about them over coffee.

steps.title: 길 묻기
steps.scene_desc: 동네 큰길 횡단보도 앞. 휴대폰 지도를 들고 두리번거리는 지우에게 대니얼이 손으로 방향을 가리켜 줌. 신호등과 표지판(글자 없음)
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "Where is the library?" (길 묻기). Goal: 길을 묻고 간단히 알려 주기. Today's scene: 동네 큰길 횡단보도 앞. 휴대폰 지도를 들고 두리번거리는 지우에게 대니얼이 손으로 방향을 가리켜 줌. 신호등과 표지판(글자 없음). Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above).
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "Excuse me. Where is the ___?".

steps.extra: Excuse me. Where is the library?
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "Excuse me. Where is the ___?" (실례합니다. ~가 어디예요?). When to use it: 모르는 사람에게 길을 물어요. Note: Excuse me. Where is the library?
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "Go straight and turn ___.".

Then go in order, one line at a time: call highlight_line with the line number before each line, read your line, and for the learner's line just wait for them to say it. If they say only part of it, say that line once and let them try once more, then go on. After the last line, give one short warm comment on how they did, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick true/false check about the scene.

items: Jiwoo is looking for the library.
The library is next to the bank.
The entrance is on the left.
steps.teach:
True/false check. The statements on the learner's screen:
1. Jiwoo is looking for the library.
2. The library is next to the bank.
3. The entrance is on the left.
The scene they are about:
1. Jiwoo: "Excuse me, sir… Oh, Daniel! Hi!" (실례합니다, 저기요… 어, 대니얼! 안녕하세요!)
2. Daniel: "Jiwoo! Are you lost?" (지우! 길 잃었어요?)
3. Jiwoo: "A little. Where is the new library?" (조금요. 새 도서관이 어디예요?)
4. Daniel: "It’s close. Go straight and turn left at the light." (가까워요. 쭉 가다가 신호등에서 왼쪽으로 돌아요.)
5. Jiwoo: "Turn left at the light. Okay." (신호등에서 왼쪽. 알겠어요.)
6. Daniel: "Then walk two blocks. It’s next to the post office." (그리고 두 블록 걸어가요. 우체국 옆에 있어요.)
7. Jiwoo: "Is it far from here?" (여기서 멀어요?)
8. Daniel: "No. About five minutes. The entrance is on your left." (아뇨. 5분쯤이에요. 입구는 왼쪽에 있어요.)
9. Jiwoo: "Thanks! The map on my phone is so confusing." (고마워요! 휴대폰 지도가 너무 헷갈려요.)
10. Daniel: "Here’s a tip. Ask people rather than your map!" (팁 하나. 지도보다 사람한테 물어봐요!)
11. Jiwoo: "Ha! Good idea. Thanks for your help!" (하하! 좋은 생각이에요. 도와줘서 고마워요!)
12. Daniel: "Anytime. You can’t miss it!" (언제든지요. 금방 찾을 거예요!)
Before you judge an answer, check the scene lines carefully: who said what. Ask one statement at a time: read it yourself and ask True or false?. Accept true/false, yes/no, or Korean (맞아요/아니에요). Say whether they are right and point to the line that shows it in a few words, also when they are right. In Korean say the answer as 정답은 True예요 / 정답은 False예요. There are 3 statements: ask every one and wait for an answer to each (Oh or Hmm is not an answer). Only after you have checked the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a table of useful sentences for real situations.

frame: Go straight and turn ___. It’s next to the ___.
head: 길 안내
뜻
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: Excuse me. Where is the ___? / Go straight and turn ___. It’s next to the ___. Table (길 안내 → 뜻):
- Go straight. → 쭉 가세요.
- Turn left. / Turn right. → 왼쪽으로 / 오른쪽으로 도세요.
- Walk two blocks. → 두 블록 걸어가세요.
- It’s on your left. → 왼쪽에 있어요.
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
동사로 바로 시작해요. 무례한 말이 아니에요.
*Go* straight. *Turn* right. *Walk* two blocks.
부드럽게: *Just* go straight.

*next to* ~ 옆 · *between* A and B A와 B 사이
*behind* ~ 뒤 · *opposite* ~ 맞은편
It’s next to the post office.
errors: Go straight and turn to left.
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- 길 안내는 명령문: 동사로 바로 시작해요. 무례한 말이 아니에요. / Go straight. Turn right. Walk two blocks. / 부드럽게: Just go straight.
- 위치 말하기: next to ~ 옆 · between A and B A와 B 사이 / behind ~ 뒤 · opposite ~ 맞은편 / It’s next to the post office.
Common mistakes on screen:
- Go straight and turn to left. → Go straight and turn left. (turn left. to를 넣지 않아요.)
- It’s next the bank. → It’s next to the bank. (next 뒤에 to를 넣어요.)
- Where is library? → Where is the library? (찾는 곳 앞에 the를 넣어요.)
- Thanks for your helping. → Thanks for your help. (your 뒤에는 help 그대로.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. After that, go over each remaining mistake on screen in one short sentence (the wrong one, the right one and why), so that no mistake on screen is skipped. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.

steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) bank / next to the café → Where is the bank? — It’s next to the café. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: bank → next to the café | bakery → behind the library | station → between the bank and the park | pharmacy → opposite the market.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to their answer, praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

This is the start of session 2 of "Where is the library?" (길 묻기); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say. Start the review only after the learner has answered at least two of your small-talk questions.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "Excuse me. Where is the ___?" / "Go straight and turn ___." / "It’s next to the ___.". One at a time: give a tiny real situation, wait for their answer and react naturally, then the next. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

groups: It’s at the end of the street.
steps.teach:
More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 방향: "Turn left." (왼쪽으로 도세요., 보통); "Turn right." (오른쪽으로 도세요., 보통); "Walk two blocks." (두 블록 가세요., 보통); "It’s on your left." (왼쪽에 있어요., 보통); "It’s at the end of the street." (길 끝에 있어요., 보통)
- 묻고 고마워하기: "Is it far from here?" (여기서 멀어요?, 보통); "I’m not from around here." (저도 이 동네 사람이 아니에요., 보통); "Thanks for your help." (도와줘서 고마워요., 보통)
- 안심시키기: "You can’t miss it." (금방 찾을 거예요., 친근)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life and take them one per turn: say one, wait for the learner to say it and react, then the next. Then use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

boxes: 길에서 보는 것

light 신호등 · crossing 횡단보도 · sign 표지판

steps.teach:
Tips on screen:
- 길에서 보는 것: light 신호등 · crossing 횡단보도 · sign 표지판 / road 도로 · block 블록(길과 길 사이) · entrance 입구
- sir · ma’am: 모르는 사람을 정중하게 부를 때: / Excuse me, sir. (남자) · Excuse me, ma’am. (여자) / 그냥 Excuse me.만 해도 충분해요.
Fill-in-the-blank dialogue on screen: A: Excuse me. ___ is the bank? B: Go ___ and turn right. / A: Is it far? B: No. It’s next ___ the café. / 낱말 상자: Where · straight · to
Mention each tip in one or two sentences, linked to the learner if you can. Then do the fill-in-the-blank dialogue: read it line by line, one blank per turn: stop at the blank, wait for them to fill it, and confirm. Then call next_step.

Picture words on screen. New: straight (쭉, 곧장), turn (돌다), block (블록), map (지도), between (~ 사이에), behind (~ 뒤에), opposite (~ 맞은편에), sign (표지판), light (신호등), crossing (횡단보도), road (도로), left (왼쪽).

Now and then ask a tiny real question with the word (for example: Are you a morning person?) and react to the answer. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a word list.

Word list on screen: end (끝) — "the end of the street"; way (길, 방법) — "Is this the way?"; miss (놓치다) — "You can’t miss it."; from (~에서(부터)) — "far from here"; address (주소) — "What’s the address?"; entrance (입구) — "the main entrance"; sir ((남자를 정중히 부를 때)) — "Excuse me, sir."; right (오른쪽(앞에서는 ‘바로’)) — "Turn right."; certainly (물론이죠, 확실히) — "Can you help me? — Certainly!".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): questions about the learner's own life.

items: You’re lost. What do you say?

steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "You’re lost. What do you say?" (hint on screen: Excuse me. Where is the ___?)
- "Tell me the way: go straight, then turn right." (hint on screen: Go straight and turn right.)
- "Is the library next to the bank or behind it? Pick one." (hint on screen: It’s next to the bank. / It’s behind the bank.)
- "Someone helps you. What do you say?" (hint on screen: Thanks for your help.)
- "Someone asks you the way. You don’t know. What do you say?" (hint on screen: Sorry, I’m not from around here.)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.

steps.title: The Old Map
steps.text: Jiwoo looks for the new library. She uses the map on her phone *rather than* asking people. She walks a block *or two*. Then she turns left. *No one* is there. It’s a parking lot! It *turns out* the map is old. Then she meets Daniel. He shows her the way. The library is right next to the post office.

Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "What does Jiwoo find at first?" / "Where is the library?". steps.title: 우리 동네
steps.title_en: Is there a bakery near here?
steps.scene_desc: 토요일 오후, 지우네 동네 길모퉁이. 지우와 놀러 온 마야가 함께 걷고, 길에는 빵집·약국·도서관·은행이 보임(간판 글자 없음)
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "Is there a bakery near here?" (우리 동네). Goal: 동네에 무엇이 있는지 묻고 말하기. Today's scene: 토요일 오후, 지우네 동네 길모퉁이. 지우와 놀러 온 마야가 함께 걷고, 길에는 빵집·약국·도서관·은행이 보임(간판 글자 없음). Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above).
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "Is there a ___ near here?".

steps.extra: Is there a bakery near here?
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "Is there a ___ near here?" (이 근처에 ~ 있어요?). When to use it: 가까이에 어떤 곳이 있는지 물어요. Note: Is there a bakery near here?
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "There’s a ___ on ___ Street.".

steps.teach:
The app has just played this scene, "A Walk with Maya · 토요일, 동네 길에서", in the characters' own voices. The learner heard it and sees it on screen:

4. Jiwoo: "Yes! There’s a bakery on Pine Street." (네! 파인 거리에 빵집이 있어요.)
5. Maya: "Is it far?" (멀어요?)
6. Jiwoo: "No, it’s really close. It’s a five-minute walk." (아뇨, 정말 가까워요. 걸어서 5분이에요.)
7. Maya: "Great. Is there a bank around here, too?" (좋아요. 이 근처에 은행도 있어요?)
8. Jiwoo: "Yes. It’s across from the library." (네. 도서관 건너편에 있어요.)
9. Maya: "And a gym? Tell me more!" (헬스장은요? 더 알려 줘요!)
10. Jiwoo: "Sorry, there isn’t a gym. But there’s a nice café around the corner." (아쉽지만 헬스장은 없어요. 그래도 모퉁이에 좋은 카페가 있어요.)
11. Maya: "Perfect. Bread and coffee!" (완벽해요. 빵이랑 커피!)

Role reading of the same scene. The learner is Jiwoo; you read the lines of Maya exactly as written, word for word. Never change, add or skip a line, and never read the learner's lines for them first.
1. Maya (you): "Jiwoo, I love this area! It’s a quiet neighborhood." (지우, 이 동네 정말 좋아요! 조용한 동네네요.)
2. Jiwoo (learner): "Thanks! There are a lot of restaurants, too." (고마워요! 식당도 많아요.)
3. Maya (you): "Nice. Is there a bakery near here? I want some bread." (좋네요. 이 근처에 빵집 있어요? 빵 좀 사고 싶어요.)
4. Jiwoo (learner): "Yes! There’s a bakery on Pine Street." (네! 파인 거리에 빵집이 있어요.)
5. Maya (you): "Is it far?" (멀어요?)
6. Jiwoo (learner): "No, it’s really close. It’s a five-minute walk." (아뇨, 정말 가까워요. 걸어서 5분이에요.)
7. Maya (you): "Great. Is there a bank around here, too?" (좋아요. 이 근처에 은행도 있어요?)
8. Jiwoo (learner): "Yes. It’s across from the library." (네. 도서관 건너편에 있어요.)
9. Maya (you): "And a gym? Tell me more!" (헬스장은요? 더 알려 줘요!)
10. Jiwoo (learner): "Sorry, there isn’t a gym. But there’s a nice café around the corner." (아쉽지만 헬스장은 없어요. 그래도 모퉁이에 좋은 카페가 있어요.)
11. Maya (you): "Perfect. Bread and coffee!" (완벽해요. 빵이랑 커피!)
First say in one short sentence that they will be Jiwoo and you will read Maya. Then go in order, one line at a time: call highlight_line with the line number before each line, read your line, and for the learner's line just wait for them to say it. If they say only part of it, say that line once and let them try once more, then go on. After the last line, give one short warm comment on how they did, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick true/false check about the scene.

Say whether they are right and point to the line that shows it in a few words, also when they are right. In Korean say the answer as 정답은 True예요 / 정답은 False예요. steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: Is there a ___ near here? / There’s a ___ on ___ Street. It’s really close. Table (있는 곳 → 위치):
- bakery 빵집 → on Pine Street
- pharmacy 약국 → around the corner
- library 도서관 → across from the bank
- restaurants 식당들 → on Main Street
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
하나: *There’s* a bank. (There is)
여럿: *There are* a lot of restaurants.
없을 때: There *isn’t* a park.

물을 땐 is를 앞으로.
*Is there* a bank near here?
— Yes, there is. / No, there isn’t.
errors: There is a lot of restaurants.
There are a lot of restaurants.
Is there a bank near here?
There’s a bakery in Pine Street.

steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- There is · There are: 하나: There’s a bank. (There is) / 여럿: There are a lot of restaurants. / 없을 때: There isn’t a park.
- Is there ~?: 물을 땐 is를 앞으로. / Is there a bank near here? / — Yes, there is. / No, there isn’t.
Common mistakes on screen:
- There is a lot of restaurants. → There are a lot of restaurants. (여럿이면 There are.)
- Is there bank near here? → Is there a bank near here? (하나일 땐 a를 넣어요.)
- There’s a bakery in Pine Street. → There’s a bakery on Pine Street. (미국 영어는 ~ Street 앞에 on. (영국 영어는 in도 써요 — 지역 차이))
- There isn’t no park. → There isn’t a park. (isn’t에 이미 ‘없다’ 뜻이 있어요.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. After that, go over each remaining mistake on screen in one short sentence (the wrong one, the right one and why), so that no mistake on screen is skipped. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.

steps.note: 예) café / around the corner → Is there a café near here? — Yes. There’s a café around the corner.
steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) café / around the corner → Is there a café near here? — Yes. There’s a café around the corner. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: café → around the corner | bank → on Oak Street | market → across from the station | library → next to the park.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to their answer, praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

This is the start of session 2 of "Is there a bakery near here?" (우리 동네); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say. Start the review only after the learner has answered at least two of your small-talk questions.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "Is there a ___ near here?" / "There’s a ___ on ___ Street." / "It’s really close.". One at a time: give a tiny real situation, wait for their answer and react naturally, then the next. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

More expressions on this topic (on screen):

Picture words on screen. New: street (거리), corner (모퉁이), market (시장, 마트), bakery (빵집), café (카페), library (도서관), pharmacy (약국), post office (우체국), police station (경찰서), fire station (소방서), church (교회). Review words: restaurant (식당).

Word list on screen: neighborhood (동네) — "a quiet neighborhood"; area (지역, 동네) — "this area"; across (건너편에) — "across from the bank"; center (중심, 센터) — "the city center"; nearby (근처의, 근처에) — "a nearby market"; bank (은행) — "Is there a bank?"; park (공원) — "Grace walks in the park every morning."; office (사무실, ~국) — "post office 우체국"; quiet (조용한) — "a quiet street".

steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "What does he do?" (그 사람은요?). Goal: 다른 사람이 하는 일과 좋아하는 것을 말하기. Today's scene: 점심시간, 회사 탕비실. 클로이와 지우가 머그잔을 들고, 지우가 휴대폰 속 이웃들 단체 사진(벤·그레이스)을 보여 줌. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above).
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "What does ___ do?".

steps.extra: What does Ben do? — He’s a teacher.
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "What does ___ do?" (~는 무슨 일 해요?). When to use it: 다른 사람이 하는 일을 물어요. Note: What does Ben do? — He’s a teacher.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "She works at ___.".

steps.title: My Neighbors · 점심시간, 회사 탕비실에서

lines.en: Ooh, who are they? Your neighbors?
Yes! This is Ben. He lives on the third floor.
{{What does}} he {{do}}?
He’s a teacher. He teaches English. He’s really funny.
And this woman?
That’s Grace. {{She works at}} the same school.
Does she have a car?
No, she doesn’t. She walks everywhere.
And Ben? What does he do on weekends?
{{He likes}} cook{{ing}}. He always says, “No worries!”
They’re very kind!
Yes. I mean, we help each other a lot.

steps.teach:
The app has just played this scene, "My Neighbors · 점심시간, 회사 탕비실에서", in the characters' own voices. The learner heard it and sees it on screen:
1. Chloe: "Ooh, who are they? Your neighbors?" (오, 이분들 누구예요? 이웃들이에요?)
2. Jiwoo: "Yes! This is Ben. He lives on the third floor." (네! 이분은 벤이에요. 3층에 살아요.)
3. Chloe: "What does he do?" (무슨 일 해요?)
4. Jiwoo: "He’s a teacher. He teaches English. He’s really funny." (선생님이에요. 영어를 가르쳐요. 정말 재미있어요.)
5. Chloe: "And this woman?" (그리고 이분은요?)
6. Jiwoo: "That’s Grace. She works at the same school." (그레이스예요. 같은 학원에서 일해요.)
7. Chloe: "Does she have a car?" (그레이스는 차 있어요?)
8. Jiwoo: "No, she doesn’t. She walks everywhere." (아뇨, 없어요. 어디든 걸어 다녀요.)
9. Chloe: "And Ben? What does he do on weekends?" (벤은요? 주말에 뭐 해요?)
10. Jiwoo: "He likes cooking. He always says, “No worries!”" (요리하는 걸 좋아해요. 늘 “괜찮아요!”라고 말해요.)
11. Chloe: "They’re very kind!" (다들 정말 친절하네요!)
12. Jiwoo: "Yes. I mean, we help each other a lot." (네. 그러니까, 우리는 서로 많이 도와요.)
Talk about it like a person: a short natural reaction, then one simple question about what happened (the answer is in the lines above). React to their answer; if it is not right, point kindly to the line that shows it. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): role reading of that scene.

steps.title: My Neighbors · 점심시간, 회사 탕비실에서

steps.teach:

12. Jiwoo (learner): "Yes. I mean, we help each other a lot." (네. 그러니까, 우리는 서로 많이 도와요.)
First say in one short sentence that they will be Jiwoo and you will read Chloe. Then go in order, one line at a time: call highlight_line with the line number before each line, read your line, and for the learner's line just wait for them to say it. If they say only part of it, say that line once and let them try once more, then go on. After the last line, give one short warm comment on how they did, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick true/false check about the scene.

Before you judge an answer, check the scene lines carefully: who said what. Ask one statement at a time: read it yourself and ask True or false?. Accept true/false, yes/no, or Korean (맞아요/아니에요). Say whether they are right and point to the line that shows it in a few words, also when they are right. In Korean say the answer as 정답은 True예요 / 정답은 False예요. There are 3 statements: ask every one and wait for an answer to each (Oh or Hmm is not an answer). Only after you have checked the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a table of useful sentences for real situations.

head: I · You
He · She
이렇게 말해요
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: What does ___ do? / She works at ___. / He likes ___ing. Table (I · You → He · She):
- I work → He works
- I like → He likes
- I go → He goes
- I have → He has
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
he·she·이름 하나 뒤에서는 동사에 *-s*.
She work*s* at a school. · Ben like*s* cooking.
go → go*es* · have → *has*

물을 때: *Does* she have a car? — Yes, she *does*.
아닐 때: He *doesn’t* like coffee.
does 뒤 동사에는 s를 붙이지 않아요.
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- 3인칭 -s: he·she·이름 하나 뒤에서는 동사에 -s. / She works at a school. · Ben likes cooking. / go → goes · have → has
- does · doesn’t: 물을 때: Does she have a car? — Yes, she does. / 아닐 때: He doesn’t like coffee. / does 뒤 동사에는 s를 붙이지 않아요.
Common mistakes on screen:
- She work at a bank. → She works at a bank. (she 뒤에는 works.)
- He haves a car. → He has a car. (have는 has로 바뀌어요.)
- Does she has a car? → Does she have a car? (does 뒤에는 동사 그대로.)
- He don’t like coffee. → He doesn’t like coffee. (he 뒤에는 doesn’t.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. After that, go over each remaining mistake on screen in one short sentence (the wrong one, the right one and why), so that no mistake on screen is skipped. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.

mistakes: She work at a bank. → She works at a bank.
He haves a car. → He has a car.

steps.note: 예) Grace / teach English → Grace teaches English. · 선생님이 묻고 내가 문장으로 대답해요.
steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) Grace / teach English → Grace teaches English. · 선생님이 묻고 내가 문장으로 대답해요. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: Grace → teach English | Daniel → go to the gym | Maya → work at an IT company | Ben → like cooking.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to their answer, praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

This is the start of session 2 of "What does he do?" (그 사람은요?); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say. Start the review only after the learner has answered at least two of your small-talk questions.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "What does ___ do?" / "She works at ___." / "He likes ___ing.". One at a time: give a tiny real situation, wait for their answer and react naturally, then the next. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

groups: He goes to the gym every day.
steps.teach:
More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 사는 곳·하는 일: "He lives in ___." (~에 살아요., 보통); "She teaches English." (영어를 가르쳐요., 보통); "He goes to the gym every day." (매일 헬스장에 가요., 보통)
- 묻고 대답하기: "Does she have a car?" (차 있어요?, 보통); "Yes, she does." (네, 있어요., 보통); "He doesn’t like ___." (~를 안 좋아해요., 보통)
- 사람 말하기: "She always says ___." (늘 ~라고 말해요., 보통); "They’re very kind." (정말 친절해요., 보통); "He’s really funny." (정말 재미있어요., 친근)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life and take them one per turn: say one, wait for the learner to say it and react, then the next. Then use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

boxes: 사람을 말하는 말

steps.teach:
Tips on screen:
- 사람을 말하는 말: coworker 직장 동료 · boss 상사 · friend 친구 / guy 남자(친근한 말) · boy 남자아이 · girl 여자아이
- 성격 말하기: funny 재미있는 · quiet 조용한 · smart 똑똑한 · kind 친절한 / He’s really funny. 정말 재미있어요.
Fill-in-the-blank dialogue on screen: A: What ___ Ben do? B: He ___ English. / A: Does he have a car? B: No, he ___. / 낱말 상자: does · teaches · doesn’t
Mention each tip in one or two sentences, linked to the learner if you can. Then do the fill-in-the-blank dialogue: read it line by line, one blank per turn: stop at the blank, wait for them to fill it, and confirm. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): picture words.

Picture words on screen. New: he (그(남자)), she (그녀(여자)), they (그들), friend (친구), coworker (직장 동료), boss (상사), gym (헬스장), funny (재미있는), smart (똑똑한), boy (남자아이), girl (여자아이). Review words: quiet (조용한).
Go through about six, new ones first, one word per turn: call highlight_word with the word, say it, and wait for the learner to say it before the next word. Never give several words in one turn. Now and then ask a tiny real question with the word (for example: Are you a morning person?) and react to the answer. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a word list.

items: do의 he·she형(하다); 질문을 만들 때도 써요
She does yoga. · What does he do?
steps.teach:
Word list on screen: does (do의 he·she형(하다); 질문을 만들 때도 써요) — "She does yoga. · What does he do?"; has ((he·she가) 가지다) — "She has a car."; goes ((he·she가) 가다) — "He goes to the gym."; guy (남자, 사람(친근)) — "a nice guy"; couple (둘, 두어 개) — "a couple of days"; strong (힘센, 강한) — "He’s strong."; single (단 하나의) — "every single day 하루도 빠짐없이"; marry (결혼하다) — "get married 결혼하다"; mate (친구(영국식)) — "He’s my mate.".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): questions about the learner's own life.

items: Tell me about a friend. What does he or she do?
He’s a ___. / She works at a ___.
Does your friend have a car?
Yes, he does. / No, she doesn’t.
Is your friend funny or quiet?
What does she do? / Does she like ___?
steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "Tell me about a friend. What does he or she do?" (hint on screen: He’s a ___. / She works at a ___.)
- "What does your friend like?" (hint on screen: He likes ___. / She likes ___ing.)
- "Does your friend have a car?" (hint on screen: Yes, he does. / No, she doesn’t.)
- "Is your friend funny or quiet?" (hint on screen: He’s really funny. / She’s quiet.)
- "Ask me about my coworker." (hint on screen: What does she do? / Does she like ___?)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.

steps.title: Grace and Ben
steps.text: Grace and Ben are coworkers. They teach English at the same school. Grace is quiet and smart. Ben is funny and *strong*. They help *each other* every *single* day. This month, Grace’s friend gets married. Grace looks for a gift for a *couple* of days. At last, she *manages to* find a nice one. Ben says, “Great gift, Grace!”
steps.gloss: strong 힘센 · each other 서로 · single 하나의 · get married 결혼하다 · a couple of 두어 · manage to 겨우 ~해내다 · at last 마침내

What does Grace find?

Reading on screen: "Grace and Ben". Text: "Grace and Ben are coworkers. They teach English at the same school. Grace is quiet and smart. Ben is funny and strong. Ben says, “Great gift, Grace!”" Words: strong 힘센 · each other 서로 · single 하나의 · get married 결혼하다 · a couple of 두어 · manage to 겨우 ~해내다 · at last 마침내.
Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "What do Grace and Ben do?" / "What does Grace find?". React to their answers; if one is not right, point to the sentence. You may add one short personal question linked to the reading. Then call next_step.

Check-out. The 'I can' list on screen:

Ask the learner to pick one and show it by saying a sentence; react and praise specifically. Then end like a person: ask how this lesson felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to it, say that the next lesson is waiting for next time, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

steps.title: 집안일
steps.title_en: Can you take out the trash?
steps.scene_desc: 저녁, 벤의 부엌. 이웃들과 저녁을 먹은 뒤 지우가 싱크대에서 설거지하고, 벤이 행주로 식탁을 닦음. 싱크대에 그릇이 쌓여 있음
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "Can you take out the trash?" (집안일). Goal: 집안일을 누가 하는지 말하고 부탁하기. Today's scene: 저녁, 벤의 부엌. 이웃들과 저녁을 먹은 뒤 지우가 싱크대에서 설거지하고, 벤이 행주로 식탁을 닦음. 싱크대에 그릇이 쌓여 있음. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above).
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "Do you cook at home?".

steps.extra: Yes, I do. / No, I don’t.
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "Do you cook at home?" (집에서 요리해요?). When to use it: 집에서 하는 일을 물어요. Note: Yes, I do. / No, I don’t.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "I do the dishes.".

steps.extra: I do the laundry. · I do the dishes.
steps.teach:
Expression 2 of 3: "I do the dishes." (제가 설거지해요.). When to use it: 집안일은 do + 일로 말해요. Note: I do the laundry. · I do the dishes.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "Can you take out the trash?".

steps.en: Can you take out the trash?
steps.extra: 대답: Sure! / Of course.
steps.teach:
Expression 3 of 3: "Can you take out the trash?" (쓰레기 좀 내다 줄래요?). When to use it: 집안일을 부탁해요. Note: 대답: Sure! / Of course.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the app plays a short scene ("After Dinner · 저녁, 벤의 부엌에서") in the characters' own voices — tell them to just listen.

steps.title: After Dinner · 저녁, 벤의 부엌에서

lines.en: Great dinner, everyone! Okay… now the dishes.
Let me help you. {{I do the dishes}} at home every day.
No worries. You’re my guest!
It’s okay. {{Do you cook at home}} every day?
Yes. In fact, I love cooking. But I hate cleaning.

lines.en: Ha! Look, the sink is full.
I know. I’ll wipe the table. It’s a little dirty.
lines.ko: 그러게요. 제가 식탁을 닦을게요. 좀 지저분하네요.

lines.en: Okay. And the trash?
Oh, {{can you take out the trash}}? It’s by the door.

Me again. You pick up the dessert!

steps.teach:

steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: Who does the ___? / I do the ___. / I make the ___. Table (do + 일 → make + 만드는 것):
- do the dishes 설거지 → make the bed 이불 정리
- do the laundry 빨래 → make dinner 저녁 만들기
- do the housework 집안일 → make lunch 점심 만들기
- do the ironing 다림질 → make coffee 커피 만들기
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.

items:
*do* + 집안일: do the dishes · do the laundry
*make* + 만드는 것: make dinner · make coffee
make the bed는 ‘이불을 정리하다’예요.

더 부드럽게: Can you *please* …?
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- do · make: do + 집안일: do the dishes · do the laundry / make + 만드는 것: make dinner · make coffee / make the bed는 ‘이불을 정리하다’예요.
- Can you ~? 부탁: Can you take out the trash? 쓰레기 좀 내다 줄래요? / 대답: Sure. / Of course. / Sorry, I’m busy. / 더 부드럽게: Can you please …?
Common mistakes on screen:
- I make the dishes. → I do the dishes. (설거지는 do the dishes.)
- I do the bed. → I make the bed. (이불 정리는 make the bed.)
- I cleaning my room. → I clean my room. (평소 하는 일은 동사 그대로.)
- Who do the cooking? → Who does the cooking? (Who가 주어면 does.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. After that, go over each remaining mistake on screen in one short sentence (the wrong one, the right one and why), so that no mistake on screen is skipped. Keep it light, then call next_step.

Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. steps.title: Ben’s Kitchen
steps.text: Ben lives alone. He loves cooking, but he hates cleaning. *In fact*, he cleans only on Sundays. He folds the sheets, sweeps the floor, and dusts the shelf. There is not a single *stain* in his kitchen. When friends visit, he cooks for them. Ben says, “Guests *are expected to* relax!” But Jiwoo always does the dishes, and she *picks up* dessert on the way.

steps.scene_desc: 옷 가게 탈의실 앞 거울. 클로이가 너무 큰 셔츠를 입고 웃고, 지우가 옆에서 웃으며 보고, 직원(조연)이 M 사이즈 셔츠를 들고 옴
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "Can I try this on?" (옷 사기). Goal: 옷을 입어 보고 사이즈를 바꿔 달라고 하기. Today's scene: 옷 가게 탈의실 앞 거울. 클로이가 너무 큰 셔츠를 입고 웃고, 지우가 옆에서 웃으며 보고, 직원(조연)이 M 사이즈 셔츠를 들고 옴. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above).
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "Can I try this on?".

steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "Can I try this on?" (이거 입어 봐도 돼요?). When to use it: 옷·신발을 입어 보고 싶을 때 써요. Note: Can I try these shoes on?
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "It’s too big.".

steps.teach:

- It’s too big. → Do you have it in a smaller size?
- It’s too small. → Do you have it in a larger size?
- It’s too tight. → Do you have a bigger one?

Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.

items:

좋은 뜻의 ‘정말’은 very·really: It’s really nice.

try *this* on — this·it은 try와 on 사이에.
small → small*er* · large → large*r* · big → big*ger*

errors: it·this 하나만 쓸 땐 try와 on 사이에. (try on this shirt는 괜찮아요)

steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- too + 형용사: ‘너무 ~해서 안 맞아요’는 too. / It’s too big. 너무 커요. · It’s too tight. 너무 껴요. / 좋은 뜻의 ‘정말’은 very·really: It’s really nice.
- try on · 더 ~한: try this on — this·it은 try와 on 사이에. / small → smaller · large → larger · big → bigger / a smaller size 더 작은 사이즈
Common mistakes on screen:
- Can I try on it? → Can I try it on? (it·this 하나만 쓸 땐 try와 on 사이에. (try on this shirt는 괜찮아요))
- It’s too much big. → It’s too big. (too 하나로 ‘너무’.)
- Do you have it in a more small size? → Do you have it in a smaller size? (small → smaller.)
- It looks well on you. → It looks good on you. (‘어울려요’는 looks good.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. After that, go over each remaining mistake on screen in one short sentence (the wrong one, the right one and why), so that no mistake on screen is skipped. Keep it light, then call next_step.

steps.title: Chloe’s Shopping Day
steps.text: Chloe loves clothes. Today she goes to a *clothing* store with Jiwoo. She tries on a shirt *as well as* a skirt. The shirt is too big, but the medium fits well. She wants a *leather* belt *as well*. Then she *finds out* the belts are on sale. “Lucky me!” she says. The total is forty thousand won. It’s *certainly* a good day!

steps.title: 장보기
steps.scene_desc: 토요일 아침, 그레이스의 부엌. 열린 냉장고 앞에서 그레이스와 지우가 메모지에 장보기 목록을 씀(글자는 보이지 않게)
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "We need some milk." (장보기). Goal: 필요한 것을 말하고 수량을 묻기. Today's scene: 토요일 아침, 그레이스의 부엌. 열린 냉장고 앞에서 그레이스와 지우가 메모지에 장보기 목록을 씀(글자는 보이지 않게). Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above).
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.

frame: We need some ___. / Is there any ___?
How many ___ do we need? / How much ___?
head: 셀 수 있는 것
셀 수 없는 것
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: We need some ___. / Is there any ___? / How many ___ do we need? / How much ___? Table (셀 수 있는 것 → 셀 수 없는 것):
- How many eggs? → How much sugar?
- a few onions → a little salt
- a lot of potatoes → a lot of milk
- two bottles of juice → some butter
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
필요하다·있다: We need *some* milk.
물을 때·없을 때: Is there *any* milk?
There isn’t *any* milk.

셀 수 있는 것: How *many* eggs?
셀 수 없는 것: How *much* sugar?
둘 다 쓸 수 있어요: a lot of
errors: How much eggs do we need?
How many eggs do we need?
우유의 양을 일반적으로 말할 때: some milk. 한 병이면: a bottle of milk.
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- some · any: 필요하다·있다: We need some milk. / 물을 때·없을 때: Is there any milk? / There isn’t any milk.
- many · much: 셀 수 있는 것: How many eggs? / 셀 수 없는 것: How much sugar? / 둘 다 쓸 수 있어요: a lot of
Common mistakes on screen:
- How much eggs do we need? → How many eggs do we need? (eggs는 셀 수 있어서 many.)
- We need a milk. → We need some milk. (우유의 양을 일반적으로 말할 때: some milk. 한 병이면: a bottle of milk.)
- There isn’t no butter. → There isn’t any butter. (isn’t 뒤에는 any.)
- two bottle of juice → two bottles of juice (둘이면 bottles.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. After that, go over each remaining mistake on screen in one short sentence (the wrong one, the right one and why), so that no mistake on screen is skipped. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.

Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) eggs / 12 → How many eggs do we need? — We need twelve. (a dozen). Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: eggs → 12 | onions → 3 | milk → 2 bottles | potatoes → 5.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to their answer, praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

This is the start of session 2 of "We need some milk." (장보기); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say. Start the review only after the learner has answered at least two of your small-talk questions.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "We need some ___." / "How many ___ do we need?" / "Is there any ___?". One at a time: give a tiny real situation, wait for their answer and react naturally, then the next. Then call next_step.

More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 없는 것 말하기: "We’re out of milk." (우유가 떨어졌어요., 보통); "Let’s make a list." (목록을 만들어요., 보통); "Don’t forget the eggs." (달걀 잊지 마요., 친근)
- 양 말하기: "Just a few." (몇 개만요., 보통); "A lot of ___." (~ 많이요., 보통); "Not much." (많이는 아니에요., 보통); "How much sugar?" (설탕은 얼마나요?, 보통)

Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life and take them one per turn: say one, wait for the learner to say it and react, then the next. Then use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.

Tips on screen:

Word list on screen: need (필요하다) — "We need some milk."; some (약간의) — "some butter"; any ((물음·부정) 조금이라도) — "Is there any salt?"; few (몇몇의) — "a few onions"; much (많은(셀 수 없는 것)) — "not much"; many (많은(셀 수 있는 것)) — "How many?"; enough (충분한) — "That’s enough."; plenty (넉넉함) — "plenty of cheese"; organic (유기농의) — "organic eggs"; themselves (그들 스스로) — "They cook for themselves.".

steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:

Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. steps.title: Grace’s Shopping List
steps.text: Grace always makes a list before shopping. It helps her save *not only* money but also time. She checks the *label* on every bottle. She buys *organic* eggs and a little cheese. *As a result*, her fridge is never too full or *empty*. Today she buys food for a brunch with the neighbors. On Sunday morning, Jiwoo helps her *set up* a big table.

What does Jiwoo help with?

steps.title: 생일 선물
steps.scene_desc: 회사 휴게실. 촛불을 꽂은 작은 케이크 앞에서 클로이가 놀라 웃고, 지우가 리본 달린 선물 상자를 건넴
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "This is for you." (생일 선물). Goal: 축하하며 선물을 주고 고맙다고 답하기. Today's scene: 회사 휴게실. 촛불을 꽂은 작은 케이크 앞에서 클로이가 놀라 웃고, 지우가 리본 달린 선물 상자를 건넴. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above).
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "Happy birthday!".

Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
