Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the app plays a short scene ("Surprise! · 회사 휴게실에서") in the characters' own voices — tell them to just listen.

frame: Happy birthday! This is for you.
You didn’t have to! I love it!

steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: Happy birthday! This is for you. / You didn’t have to! I love it! Table (이럴 때 → 주는 사람):
- 생일 → Happy birthday!
- 선물을 줄 때 → This is for you.
- 선물을 열고 → Open it!
- 초를 끌 때 → Make a wish!
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
This is *for* you. 이거 받아요(선물이에요).
for + 받는 사람: a gift *for* Chloe
겸손하게: It’s just a little something.

I *love* it! 정말 마음에 들어요!
It’s *perfect*. 딱이에요.
How did you know? 어떻게 알았어요?
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- This is for you.: This is for you. 이거 받아요(선물이에요). / for + 받는 사람: a gift for Chloe / 겸손하게: It’s just a little something.
- 기쁨 말하기: I love it! 정말 마음에 들어요! / It’s perfect. 딱이에요. / How did you know? 어떻게 알았어요?
Common mistakes on screen:
- This is for your. → This is for you. (for 뒤에는 you.)
- I’m love it! → I love it! (am을 넣지 않아요.)
- Congratulation birthday! → Happy birthday! (생일 축하는 Happy birthday!)
- You don’t have to! → You didn’t have to! (이미 받은 선물엔 didn’t.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. After that, go over each remaining mistake on screen in one short sentence (the wrong one, the right one and why), so that no mistake on screen is skipped. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.

steps.note: 예) Chloe / a frame → Happy birthday, Chloe! This is for you. It’s a frame.
steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) Chloe / a frame → Happy birthday, Chloe! This is for you. It’s a frame. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: Chloe → a frame | Ben → a candle | Grace → flowers | Daniel → a book.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to their answer, praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

This is the start of session 2 of "This is for you." (생일 선물); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say. Start the review only after the learner has answered at least two of your small-talk questions.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "Happy birthday!" / "This is for you." / "I love it!". One at a time: give a tiny real situation, wait for their answer and react naturally, then the next. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 받을 때: "You didn’t have to!" (안 그래도 되는데!, 보통); "What is it?" (뭐예요?, 친근); "How did you know?" (어떻게 알았어요?, 친근); "It’s perfect." (딱이에요., 보통)
- 줄 때: "Open it!" (열어 봐요!, 친근); "It’s just a little something." (작은 거예요., 보통)
- 생일 파티: "Thank you for coming." (와 줘서 고마워요., 보통); "Let’s have some cake." (케이크 먹어요., 친근); "Make a wish!" (소원 빌어요!, 친근)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life and take them one per turn: say one, wait for the learner to say it and react, then the next. Then use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

Now and then ask a tiny real question with the word (for example: Are you a morning person?) and react to the answer. Then call next_step.

Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.

How do people celebrate birthdays in Korea?
steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "When’s your birthday?" (hint on screen: It’s on ___. (예: It’s on March twelfth.))
- "What’s a good birthday present?" (hint on screen: Flowers are a good present. / A ___ is good.)
- "It’s my birthday today!" (hint on screen: Happy birthday! This is for you.)
- "I give you a gift. What do you say?" (hint on screen: Thank you! You didn’t have to! / I love it!)
- "How do people celebrate birthdays in Korea?" (hint on screen: They have cake and ___.)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.

steps.title: Chloe’s Party
steps.text: On Friday, Chloe has a small birthday party. She invites ten guests. Jiwoo brings her friends Grace, Ben, and Daniel. Grace makes a round cake, and Ben brings a big teddy *bear*. Daniel *makes up* a funny birthday poem. Everyone laughs. Chloe says, “*You see*, this is my first birthday party in Seoul. It’s so special!” Then she makes a wish and blows out the candles.
steps.gloss: teddy bear 곰 인형 · make up 지어내다 · poem 시 · you see 있잖아요, 그러니까 · blow out (불을) 끄다
questions: What does Ben bring?
Why is the party special for Chloe?
steps.teach:
Reading on screen: "Chloe’s Party". Text: "On Friday, Chloe has a small birthday party. She invites ten guests. Jiwoo brings her friends Grace, Ben, and Daniel. Grace makes a round cake, and Ben brings a big teddy bear. Daniel makes up a funny birthday poem. Everyone laughs. Chloe says, “You see, this is my first birthday party in Seoul. It’s so special!” Then she makes a wish and blows out the candles." Words: teddy bear 곰 인형 · make up 지어내다 · poem 시 · you see 있잖아요, 그러니까 · blow out (불을) 끄다.
Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "What does Ben bring?" / "Why is the party special for Chloe?". React to their answers; if one is not right, point to the sentence. You may add one short personal question linked to the reading. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the 'I can' check-out.

items: ‘This is for you.’로 선물을 건넬 수 있어요.
‘I love it!’으로 선물을 받고 기쁨을 말할 수 있어요.
steps.teach:
Check-out. The 'I can' list on screen:
- ‘Happy birthday!’로 생일을 축하할 수 있어요.
- ‘This is for you.’로 선물을 건넬 수 있어요.
- ‘I love it!’으로 선물을 받고 기쁨을 말할 수 있어요.
Ask the learner to pick one and show it by saying a sentence; react and praise specifically. Then end like a person: ask how this lesson felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to it, say that the next lesson is waiting for next time, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

steps.title: 전화하기
steps.goal: 전화로 사람을 찾고 나중에 다시 걸겠다고 하기
steps.scene_desc: 저녁, 화면 둘로 나뉨. 왼쪽: 지우가 집 소파에서 휴대폰으로 전화. 오른쪽: 어학원 안내 데스크에서 벤이 수화기를 들고 웃음
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "Can I speak to Grace?" (전화하기). Goal: 전화로 사람을 찾고 나중에 다시 걸겠다고 하기. Today's scene: 저녁, 화면 둘로 나뉨. 왼쪽: 지우가 집 소파에서 휴대폰으로 전화. 오른쪽: 어학원 안내 데스크에서 벤이 수화기를 들고 웃음. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above).
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "Hello, this is ___.".

steps.extra: Hello, this is Jiwoo.
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "Hello, this is ___." (여보세요, 저 ~예요.). When to use it: 전화로 내가 누구인지 말해요. Note: Hello, this is Jiwoo.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "Can I speak to ___?".

steps.extra: Can I speak to Grace?
steps.teach:
Expression 2 of 3: "Can I speak to ___?" (~ 좀 바꿔 주시겠어요?). When to use it: 전화로 찾는 사람을 말해요. Note: Can I speak to Grace?
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "I’ll call you back.".

Before you judge an answer, check the scene lines carefully: who said what. Ask one statement at a time: read it yourself and ask True or false?. Accept true/false, yes/no, or Korean (맞아요/아니에요). Say whether they are right and point to the line that shows it in a few words, also when they are right. In Korean say the answer as 정답은 True예요 / 정답은 False예요. frame: Hello, this is ___. Can I speak to ___?
Speaking. / Sorry, she’s not here right now.
head: 이럴 때
이렇게 말해요
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: Hello, this is ___. Can I speak to ___? / Speaking. / Sorry, she’s not here right now. Table (이럴 때 → 이렇게 말해요):
- 내가 누구인지 → Hello, this is Jiwoo.
- 바꿔 달라고 → Can I speak to Grace?
- 내가 그 사람일 때 → Speaking.
- 나중에 다시 → I’ll call you back.
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
전화로 나를 소개할 땐 보통 *This is* Jiwoo.
상대를 물을 땐: Who’s calling, please?
찾는 사람이 나일 때: Speaking.

I’ll *call* you *back*. 다시 걸게요.
*Hold on*, please. 잠시만요.
Can you ask her to call me? 전화해 달라고 전해 줄래요?
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- 전화에서는 this is: 전화로 나를 소개할 땐 보통 This is Jiwoo. / 상대를 물을 땐: Who’s calling, please? / 찾는 사람이 나일 때: Speaking.
- call back · hold on: I’ll call you back. 다시 걸게요. / Hold on, please. 잠시만요. / Can you ask her to call me? 전화해 달라고 전해 줄래요?
Common mistakes on screen:
- Can I speak Grace? → Can I speak to Grace? (speak 뒤에 to.)
- I’ll call back you. → I’ll call you back. (you는 call과 back 사이에.)
- I can’t listen you. → I can’t hear you. (들리지 않을 땐 hear.)
- She’s not here now right. → She’s not here right now. (right now는 붙여서 한 덩어리.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. After that, go over each remaining mistake on screen in one short sentence (the wrong one, the right one and why), so that no mistake on screen is skipped. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.

steps.note: 예) Grace / not here → Can I speak to Grace? — Sorry, she’s not here right now.
steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) Grace / not here → Can I speak to Grace? — Sorry, she’s not here right now. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: Grace → not here | Daniel → on another line | Maya → in a meeting | Chloe → Speaking.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to their answer, praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

This is the start of session 2 of "Can I speak to Grace?" (전화하기); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say. Start the review only after the learner has answered at least two of your small-talk questions.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "Hello, this is ___." / "Can I speak to ___?" / "I’ll call you back.". One at a time: give a tiny real situation, wait for their answer and react naturally, then the next. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

groups: Can you ask her to call me?
steps.teach:
More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 받는 사람: "Who’s calling, please?" (누구세요?, 정중); "Speaking." (전데요., 보통); "Hold on, please." (잠시만요., 보통); "He’s not here right now." (지금 없어요., 보통)
- 거는 사람: "Can you ask her to call me?" (전화해 달라고 전해 줄래요?, 보통); "Sorry, wrong number." (죄송해요, 잘못 걸었어요., 보통)
- 잘 안 들릴 때·끊을 때: "I can’t hear you." (잘 안 들려요., 보통); "Can you hear me now?" (이제 들려요?, 보통); "Talk to you later." (나중에 얘기해요., 친근)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life and take them one per turn: say one, wait for the learner to say it and react, then the next. Then use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

Picture words on screen. New: hold ((끊지 않고) 기다리다), hear (듣다, 들리다), voice (목소리), ring (울리다), mobile (휴대폰), speaker (스피커), dial (번호를 누르다), chat (수다, 이야기하다), message (메시지), number (번호), missed (놓친), answer ((전화를) 받다).

steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "I answer the phone: “Hello?” Say who you are." (hint on screen: Hello, this is ___.)
- "Ask to speak to Ben." (hint on screen: Can I speak to Ben?)
- "Ben is not here. What do you say?" (hint on screen: Can you ask him to call me? / I’ll call back later.)

- "Do you like phone calls or messages?" (hint on screen: I like ___. / Messages are easier.)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.

steps.title: A Busy Evening
steps.text: In the evening, Jiwoo calls the language school. Ben answers. Grace is on another line, so Jiwoo says, “I’ll call back later.” Ten minutes later, Grace *comes back* to her desk. Then Jiwoo’s phone rings. It’s Grace! “*Come on*, let’s have dinner!” Jiwoo is tired after *a number of* busy days. But she smiles and says, “Sure, I’d love to!”
steps.gloss: on another line 다른 통화 중 · ring 울리다 · come back 돌아오다 · come on 자, 어서 · a number of 여러
questions: Who answers the phone at the school?
What does Grace want to do?
steps.teach:
Reading on screen: "A Busy Evening". Text: "In the evening, Jiwoo calls the language school. Ben answers. Grace is on another line, so Jiwoo says, “I’ll call back later.” Ten minutes later, Grace comes back to her desk. Then Jiwoo’s phone rings. It’s Grace! “Come on, let’s have dinner!” Jiwoo is tired after a number of busy days. But she smiles and says, “Sure, I’d love to!”" Words: on another line 다른 통화 중 · ring 울리다 · come back 돌아오다 · come on 자, 어서 · a number of 여러.
Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "Who answers the phone at the school?" / "What does Grace want to do?". React to their answers; if one is not right, point to the sentence. You may add one short personal question linked to the reading. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the 'I can' check-out.

Ask the learner to pick one and show it by saying a sentence; react and praise specifically. Then end like a person: ask how this lesson felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to it, say that the next lesson is waiting for next time, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

steps.scene_desc: 월요일 아침, 동네 모퉁이 카페. 대니얼이 커피를 들고 걱정스럽게 묻고, 지우가 한 손으로 볼을 감싼 채 웃음
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "Where were you yesterday?" (어디 있었어요?). Goal: 어제 어디에 있었는지와 어땠는지 말하기. Today's scene: 월요일 아침, 동네 모퉁이 카페. 대니얼이 커피를 들고 걱정스럽게 묻고, 지우가 한 손으로 볼을 감싼 채 웃음. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above).
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "Where were you yesterday?".

steps.extra: 대답: I was at home.
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "Where were you yesterday?" (어제 어디 있었어요?). When to use it: 지난 일, 있던 곳을 물어요. Note: 대답: I was at home.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "I was at ___.".

steps.extra: I was at the dentist. · I was at work.
steps.teach:
Expression 2 of 3: "I was at ___." (~에 있었어요.). When to use it: 어제 있던 곳을 말해요. Note: I was at the dentist. · I was at work.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "I had a ___ day.".

steps.extra: I had a long day. · I had a great day.
steps.teach:
Expression 3 of 3: "I had a ___ day." (~한 하루였어요.). When to use it: 하루가 어땠는지 말해요. Note: I had a long day. · I had a great day.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the app plays a short scene ("Monday Morning · 월요일 아침, 동네 카페에서") in the characters' own voices — tell them to just listen.

steps.teach:
The app has just played this scene, "Monday Morning · 월요일 아침, 동네 카페에서", in the characters' own voices. The learner heard it and sees it on screen:
1. Daniel: "Hi, Jiwoo! Where were you yesterday? You weren’t at the café." (안녕, 지우! 어제 어디 있었어요? 카페에 안 왔던데요.)
2. Jiwoo: "I was at the dentist." (치과에 있었어요.)
3. Daniel: "The dentist? Why?" (치과요? 왜요?)
4. Jiwoo: "I had a toothache. It was a long day." (이가 아팠어요. 긴 하루였어요.)
5. Daniel: "Oh no. Was it terrible?" (저런. 끔찍했어요?)
6. Jiwoo: "It was okay. But I was so tired last night." (괜찮았어요. 그런데 어젯밤엔 너무 피곤했어요.)
7. Daniel: "Were you busy after that?" (그다음엔 바빴어요?)
8. Jiwoo: "No, I wasn’t. I was at home after that." (아뇨. 그 뒤에는 집에 있었어요.)
9. Daniel: "Good. Rest is important." (잘했어요. 쉬는 게 중요해요.)
10. Jiwoo: "What about you? Were you here?" (대니얼은요? 여기 있었어요?)
11. Daniel: "No. Grace and I were at the park. The weather was perfect." (아뇨. 그레이스랑 공원에 있었어요. 날씨가 완벽했어요.)
12. Jiwoo: "Lucky you! I had a boring day." (좋았겠다! 저는 지루한 하루였어요.)
Talk about it like a person: a short natural reaction, then one simple question about what happened (the answer is in the lines above). React to their answer; if it is not right, point kindly to the line that shows it. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): role reading of that scene.

steps.teach:
Role reading of the same scene. The learner is Jiwoo; you read the lines of Daniel exactly as written, word for word. Never change, add or skip a line, and never read the learner's lines for them first.
1. Daniel (you): "Hi, Jiwoo! Where were you yesterday? You weren’t at the café." (안녕, 지우! 어제 어디 있었어요? 카페에 안 왔던데요.)
2. Jiwoo (learner): "I was at the dentist." (치과에 있었어요.)
3. Daniel (you): "The dentist? Why?" (치과요? 왜요?)
4. Jiwoo (learner): "I had a toothache. It was a long day." (이가 아팠어요. 긴 하루였어요.)
5. Daniel (you): "Oh no. Was it terrible?" (저런. 끔찍했어요?)
6. Jiwoo (learner): "It was okay. But I was so tired last night." (괜찮았어요. 그런데 어젯밤엔 너무 피곤했어요.)
7. Daniel (you): "Were you busy after that?" (그다음엔 바빴어요?)
8. Jiwoo (learner): "No, I wasn’t. I was at home after that." (아뇨. 그 뒤에는 집에 있었어요.)
9. Daniel (you): "Good. Rest is important." (잘했어요. 쉬는 게 중요해요.)
10. Jiwoo (learner): "What about you? Were you here?" (대니얼은요? 여기 있었어요?)
11. Daniel (you): "No. Grace and I were at the park. The weather was perfect." (아뇨. 그레이스랑 공원에 있었어요. 날씨가 완벽했어요.)
12. Jiwoo (learner): "Lucky you! I had a boring day." (좋았겠다! 저는 지루한 하루였어요.)
First say in one short sentence that they will be Jiwoo and you will read Daniel. Then go in order, one line at a time: call highlight_line with the line number before each line, read your line, and for the learner's line just wait for them to say it. If they say only part of it, say that line once and let them try once more, then go on. After the last line, give one short warm comment on how they did, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick true/false check about the scene.

True/false check. The statements on the learner's screen:
1. Jiwoo was at the dentist.
2. Jiwoo was busy all day.
3. Daniel was at the park.
The scene they are about:
1. Daniel: "Hi, Jiwoo! Where were you yesterday? You weren’t at the café." (안녕, 지우! 어제 어디 있었어요? 카페에 안 왔던데요.)
2. Jiwoo: "I was at the dentist." (치과에 있었어요.)
3. Daniel: "The dentist? Why?" (치과요? 왜요?)
4. Jiwoo: "I had a toothache. It was a long day." (이가 아팠어요. 긴 하루였어요.)
5. Daniel: "Oh no. Was it terrible?" (저런. 끔찍했어요?)
6. Jiwoo: "It was okay. But I was so tired last night." (괜찮았어요. 그런데 어젯밤엔 너무 피곤했어요.)
7. Daniel: "Were you busy after that?" (그다음엔 바빴어요?)
8. Jiwoo: "No, I wasn’t. I was at home after that." (아뇨. 그 뒤에는 집에 있었어요.)
9. Daniel: "Good. Rest is important." (잘했어요. 쉬는 게 중요해요.)
10. Jiwoo: "What about you? Were you here?" (대니얼은요? 여기 있었어요?)
11. Daniel: "No. Grace and I were at the park. The weather was perfect." (아뇨. 그레이스랑 공원에 있었어요. 날씨가 완벽했어요.)
12. Jiwoo: "Lucky you! I had a boring day." (좋았겠다! 저는 지루한 하루였어요.)
Before you judge an answer, check the scene lines carefully: who said what. Ask one statement at a time: read it yourself and ask True or false?. Accept true/false, yes/no, or Korean (맞아요/아니에요). Say whether they are right and point to the line that shows it in a few words, also when they are right. In Korean say the answer as 정답은 True예요 / 정답은 False예요. There are 3 statements: ask every one and wait for an answer to each (Oh or Hmm is not an answer). Only after you have checked the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a table of useful sentences for real situations.

frame: I was at ___. I had a ___ day.
head: 지금
지난 일
이렇게 말해요
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: Where were you yesterday? / I was at ___. I had a ___ day. Table (지금 → 지난 일):
- I am → I was
- You are → You were
- He · She is → He · She was
- We · They are → We · They were
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
지난 일의 be동사: am·is → *was* · are → *were*
I *was* at the dentist.
We *were* at the park.

*Were* you busy? — Yes, I was. / No, I *wasn’t*.
*Was* it fun? 재미있었어요?
wasn’t = was not · weren’t = were not
errors: 지루한 ‘날’은 boring. bored는 사람이 지루할 때.
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- was · were: 지난 일의 be동사: am·is → was · are → were / I was at the dentist. / We were at the park.
- 물을 때·아닐 때: Were you busy? — Yes, I was. / No, I wasn’t. / Was it fun? 재미있었어요? / wasn’t = was not · weren’t = were not
Common mistakes on screen:
- I am at home yesterday. → I was at home yesterday. (어제 일은 was.)
- We was at the park. → We were at the park. (we 뒤에는 were.)
- Where you were yesterday? → Where were you yesterday? (물을 땐 were를 you 앞에.)
- It was a bored day. → It was a boring day. (지루한 ‘날’은 boring. bored는 사람이 지루할 때.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. After that, go over each remaining mistake on screen in one short sentence (the wrong one, the right one and why), so that no mistake on screen is skipped. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.

We was at the park. → We were at the park.
Where you were yesterday? → Where were you yesterday?

steps.note: 예) home / all day → Where were you yesterday? — I was at home all day.
steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) home / all day → Where were you yesterday? — I was at home all day. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: home → all day | the dentist → in the morning | work → until nine | the park → with friends.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to their answer, praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

This is the start of session 2 of "Where were you yesterday?" (어디 있었어요?); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say. Start the review only after the learner has answered at least two of your small-talk questions.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "Where were you yesterday?" / "I was at ___." / "I had a ___ day.". One at a time: give a tiny real situation, wait for their answer and react naturally, then the next. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

groups: I was at home all day.
steps.teach:
More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 어디 있었어요: "I was at home all day." (하루 종일 집에 있었어요., 보통); "We were at the park." (우리는 공원에 있었어요., 보통)
- 묻고 대답하기: "Were you busy?" (바빴어요?, 보통); "Yes, I was." (네, 바빴어요., 보통); "No, I wasn’t." (아니요., 보통); "Was it fun?" (재미있었어요?, 친근)
- 어땠어요: "It was a long day." (긴 하루였어요., 보통); "I was so tired." (너무 피곤했어요., 보통); "The weather was perfect." (날씨가 완벽했어요., 보통)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life and take them one per turn: say one, wait for the learner to say it and react, then the next. Then use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

steps.teach:
Tips on screen:
- 어땠어요? 느낌 말: wonderful · perfect 아주 좋은 · boring 지루한 / terrible · awful · horrible 끔찍한 / It was OK. 괜찮았어요.
- 지난 때를 말하는 말: yesterday 어제 · last night 어젯밤 / two days ago 이틀 전 · last week 지난주
Fill-in-the-blank dialogue on screen: A: Where ___ you yesterday? B: I ___ at the dentist. / A: ___ it terrible? B: No, it ___ okay. / 낱말 상자: were · was · Was · was
Mention each tip in one or two sentences, linked to the learner if you can. Then do the fill-in-the-blank dialogue: read it line by line, one blank per turn: stop at the blank, wait for them to fill it, and confirm. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): picture words.

Picture words on screen. New: dentist (치과 의사, 치과), hairdresser (미용사), wonderful (아주 멋진), boring (지루한), terrible (끔찍한), ago (~ 전에), home (집), yesterday (어제), night (밤), fun (재미), all day (하루 종일). Review words: perfect (완벽한).
Go through about six, new ones first, one word per turn: call highlight_word with the word, say it, and wait for the learner to say it before the next word. Never give several words in one turn. Now and then ask a tiny real question with the word (for example: Are you a morning person?) and react to the answer. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a word list.

Word list on screen: was ((am·is의 과거) ~였다) — "I was tired."; were ((are의 과거) ~였다) — "We were at home."; awful (끔찍한) — "an awful day"; horrible (끔찍한) — "a horrible cold"; last (지난) — "last night"; long (긴) — "a long day"; ok (괜찮은(= okay)) — "It was OK."; remain (남아 있다) — "Two days remain."; period (기간) — "a short period".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): questions about the learner's own life.

items: Yes, I was. / No, I wasn’t.
It was ___. I had a ___ day.
Yes, it was perfect. / No, it was terrible.
Ask me about my day yesterday.
Where were you? / Was it fun?
steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "Where were you yesterday?" (hint on screen: I was at ___.)
- "Were you busy yesterday?" (hint on screen: Yes, I was. / No, I wasn’t.)
- "How was your day yesterday?" (hint on screen: It was ___. I had a ___ day.)
- "Was the weather nice yesterday?" (hint on screen: Yes, it was perfect. / No, it was terrible.)
- "Ask me about my day yesterday." (hint on screen: Where were you? / Was it fun?)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.

steps.title: Jiwoo’s Tooth
steps.text: Jiwoo’s tooth was bad for a week. She was afraid of the dentist. But Daniel said, “Don’t *give up*. Go!” So yesterday she was at the dentist. It was not terrible. The dentist was kind. Sweets can *lead to* bad teeth, so now Jiwoo eats fewer sweets. *Last night*, she was tired but happy.
steps.gloss: afraid of ~을 무서워하는 · give up 포기하다 · lead to ~로 이어지다 · sweets 단것 · fewer 더 적은
questions: Where was Jiwoo yesterday?
Was the dentist kind?
steps.teach:
Reading on screen: "Jiwoo’s Tooth". Text: "Jiwoo’s tooth was bad for a week. She was afraid of the dentist. But Daniel said, “Don’t give up. Go!” So yesterday she was at the dentist. It was not terrible. The dentist was kind. Sweets can lead to bad teeth, so now Jiwoo eats fewer sweets. Last night, she was tired but happy." Words: afraid of ~을 무서워하는 · give up 포기하다 · lead to ~로 이어지다 · sweets 단것 · fewer 더 적은.
Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "Where was Jiwoo yesterday?" / "Was the dentist kind?". React to their answers; if one is not right, point to the sentence. You may add one short personal question linked to the reading. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the 'I can' check-out.

items: ‘Where were you yesterday?’로 어제 있던 곳을 물을 수 있어요.
‘I was at ___.’로 어제 있던 곳을 말할 수 있어요.
‘I had a ___ day.’로 하루가 어땠는지 말할 수 있어요.
steps.teach:
Check-out. The 'I can' list on screen:
- ‘Where were you yesterday?’로 어제 있던 곳을 물을 수 있어요.
- ‘I was at ___.’로 어제 있던 곳을 말할 수 있어요.
- ‘I had a ___ day.’로 하루가 어땠는지 말할 수 있어요.
Ask the learner to pick one and show it by saying a sentence; react and praise specifically. Then end like a person: ask how this lesson felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to it, say that the next lesson is waiting for next time, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

steps.title: 지난 주말
steps.title_en: What did you do last weekend?
steps.goal: 지난 주말에 한 일을 말하고 어땠는지 답하기
steps.scene_desc: 월요일 점심, 회사 근처 식당. 마야와 지우가 마주 앉아 지우의 휴대폰 속 주말 사진(아쿠아리움의 큰 물고기)을 보며 웃음
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "What did you do last weekend?" (지난 주말). Goal: 지난 주말에 한 일을 말하고 어땠는지 답하기. Today's scene: 월요일 점심, 회사 근처 식당. 마야와 지우가 마주 앉아 지우의 휴대폰 속 주말 사진(아쿠아리움의 큰 물고기)을 보며 웃음. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above).
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "What did you do last weekend?".

steps.en: What did you do last weekend?
steps.extra: 대답: I went to the zoo.
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "What did you do last weekend?" (지난 주말에 뭐 했어요?). When to use it: 지난 주말에 한 일을 물어요. Note: 대답: I went to the zoo.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "I ___. (지난 일)".

steps.extra: I visited the aquarium. · I went bowling.
steps.teach:
Expression 2 of 3: "I ___. (지난 일)" (~했어요.). When to use it: 지난 일은 동사 모양이 바뀌어요. Note: I visited the aquarium. · I went bowling.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "It was ___.".

steps.extra: It was fun. · It was amazing.
steps.teach:
Expression 3 of 3: "It was ___." (~했어요.(느낌)). When to use it: 어땠는지 말해요. Note: It was fun. · It was amazing.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the app plays a short scene ("Weekend Stories · 월요일 점심, 식당에서") in the characters' own voices — tell them to just listen.

steps.title: Weekend Stories · 월요일 점심, 식당에서

lines.en: Hi, Jiwoo! {{What did you do last weekend}}?
lines.ko: 안녕, 지우! 지난 주말에 뭐 했어요?

lines.en: {{I visited}} the aquarium with Chloe. {{It was}} amazing!
Nice! Tell me more.
We saw big fish. Then we had brunch.

No! I was sort of bad. But it was fun.

steps.teach:
The app has just played this scene, "Weekend Stories · 월요일 점심, 식당에서", in the characters' own voices. The learner heard it and sees it on screen:
1. Maya: "Hi, Jiwoo! What did you do last weekend?" (안녕, 지우! 지난 주말에 뭐 했어요?)
2. Jiwoo: "I visited the aquarium with Chloe. It was amazing!" (클로이랑 아쿠아리움에 갔어요. 정말 멋졌어요!)
3. Maya: "Nice! Tell me more." (좋네요! 더 얘기해 줘요.)
4. Jiwoo: "We saw big fish. Then we had brunch." (큰 물고기를 봤어요. 그리고 브런치를 먹었어요.)
5. Maya: "Sounds fun. Did you have a good weekend?" (재미있었겠다. 주말 잘 보냈네요?)
6. Jiwoo: "Yes, I did. How about you?" (네. 마야는요?)
7. Maya: "I went bowling on Saturday. And on Sunday, I didn’t do much." (토요일엔 볼링 치러 갔어요. 일요일엔 별로 한 게 없어요.)
8. Jiwoo: "Bowling? Did you win?" (볼링이요? 이겼어요?)
9. Maya: "No! I was sort of bad. But it was fun." (아뇨! 좀 못했어요. 그래도 재미있었어요.)
10. Jiwoo: "Ha! And on Sunday?" (하하! 일요일은요?)
11. Maya: "I stayed home and slept a lot." (집에 있으면서 잠을 많이 잤어요.)
12. Jiwoo: "That’s a good weekend, too!" (그것도 좋은 주말이네요!)
Talk about it like a person: a short natural reaction, then one simple question about what happened (the answer is in the lines above). React to their answer; if it is not right, point kindly to the line that shows it. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): role reading of that scene.

steps.teach:
Role reading of the same scene. The learner is Jiwoo; you read the lines of Maya exactly as written, word for word. Never change, add or skip a line, and never read the learner's lines for them first.
1. Maya (you): "Hi, Jiwoo! What did you do last weekend?" (안녕, 지우! 지난 주말에 뭐 했어요?)
2. Jiwoo (learner): "I visited the aquarium with Chloe. It was amazing!" (클로이랑 아쿠아리움에 갔어요. 정말 멋졌어요!)
3. Maya (you): "Nice! Tell me more." (좋네요! 더 얘기해 줘요.)
4. Jiwoo (learner): "We saw big fish. Then we had brunch." (큰 물고기를 봤어요. 그리고 브런치를 먹었어요.)
5. Maya (you): "Sounds fun. Did you have a good weekend?" (재미있었겠다. 주말 잘 보냈네요?)
6. Jiwoo (learner): "Yes, I did. How about you?" (네. 마야는요?)
7. Maya (you): "I went bowling on Saturday. And on Sunday, I didn’t do much." (토요일엔 볼링 치러 갔어요. 일요일엔 별로 한 게 없어요.)
8. Jiwoo (learner): "Bowling? Did you win?" (볼링이요? 이겼어요?)
9. Maya (you): "No! I was sort of bad. But it was fun." (아뇨! 좀 못했어요. 그래도 재미있었어요.)
10. Jiwoo (learner): "Ha! And on Sunday?" (하하! 일요일은요?)
11. Maya (you): "I stayed home and slept a lot." (집에 있으면서 잠을 많이 잤어요.)
12. Jiwoo (learner): "That’s a good weekend, too!" (그것도 좋은 주말이네요!)
First say in one short sentence that they will be Jiwoo and you will read Maya. Then go in order, one line at a time: call highlight_line with the line number before each line, read your line, and for the learner's line just wait for them to say it. If they say only part of it, say that line once and let them try once more, then go on. After the last line, give one short warm comment on how they did, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick true/false check about the scene.

True/false check. The statements on the learner's screen:
1. Jiwoo went to the aquarium.
2. Maya went to the zoo.
3. Maya stayed home on Sunday.

Before you judge an answer, check the scene lines carefully: who said what. Ask one statement at a time: read it yourself and ask True or false?. Accept true/false, yes/no, or Korean (맞아요/아니에요). Say whether they are right and point to the line that shows it in a few words, also when they are right. In Korean say the answer as 정답은 True예요 / 정답은 False예요. There are 3 statements: ask every one and wait for an answer to each (Oh or Hmm is not an answer). Only after you have checked the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a table of useful sentences for real situations.

frame: What did you do last weekend?
I visited / went / met ___. It was ___.
head: 지금
지난 일
이렇게 말해요
rows: We saw fish. We ate brunch.
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: What did you do last weekend? / I visited / went / met ___. It was ___. Table (지금 → 지난 일):
- visit → visited
- stay → stayed
- go → went
- see · eat → saw · ate
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
대부분 동사 + *-ed*: visit*ed* · stay*ed* · relax*ed*
모양이 바뀌는 동사: go → *went* · see → *saw* · eat → *ate* · meet → *met* · sleep → *slept*

물을 때: *Did* you have a good weekend? — Yes, I *did*.
아닐 때: I *didn’t* do much.
did 뒤에는 동사 그대로.
errors: I go to the movies last weekend.
I went to the movies last weekend.
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- 지난 일: -ed: 대부분 동사 + -ed: visited · stayed · relaxed / 모양이 바뀌는 동사: go → went · see → saw · eat → ate · meet → met · sleep → slept
- did · didn’t: 물을 때: Did you have a good weekend? — Yes, I did. / 아닐 때: I didn’t do much. / did 뒤에는 동사 그대로.
Common mistakes on screen:
- I go to the movies last weekend. → I went to the movies last weekend. (지난 일은 went.)
- I didn’t went out. → I didn’t go out. (didn’t 뒤에는 동사 그대로.)
- Did you had fun? → Did you have fun? (did 뒤에는 have.)
- I sleeped a lot. → I slept a lot. (sleep → slept.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. After that, go over each remaining mistake on screen in one short sentence (the wrong one, the right one and why), so that no mistake on screen is skipped. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.

steps.note: 예) go / the movies → What did you do last weekend? — I went to the movies.
steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) go / the movies → What did you do last weekend? — I went to the movies. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: go → the movies | meet → my friends | play → tennis | clean → my room.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to their answer, praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

cards: What did you do last weekend?
steps.teach:
This is the start of session 2 of "What did you do last weekend?" (지난 주말); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say. Start the review only after the learner has answered at least two of your small-talk questions.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "What did you do last weekend?" / "I ___. (지난 일)" / "It was ___.". One at a time: give a tiny real situation, wait for their answer and react naturally, then the next. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

groups: Did you have a good weekend?
steps.teach:
More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 한 일 말하기: "I went to the movies." (영화 보러 갔어요., 보통); "I stayed home." (집에 있었어요., 보통); "I met my friends." (친구들을 만났어요., 보통); "We had dinner together." (같이 저녁 먹었어요., 보통); "I slept a lot." (많이 잤어요., 친근)
- 묻고 대답하기: "Did you have a good weekend?" (주말 잘 보냈어요?, 보통); "Yes, I did." (네., 보통); "How about you?" (당신은요?, 보통)
- 별일 없을 때: "I didn’t do much." (별로 한 게 없어요., 보통)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life and take them one per turn: say one, wait for the learner to say it and react, then the next. Then use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

Tips on screen:
- 주말에 하는 것: bike ride 자전거 타기 · hike 등산 · bowling 볼링 / karaoke 노래방 · flea market 벼룩시장 · brunch 브런치

Mention each tip in one or two sentences, linked to the learner if you can. Then do the fill-in-the-blank dialogue: read it line by line, one blank per turn: stop at the blank, wait for them to fill it, and confirm. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): picture words.

Picture words on screen. New: zoo (동물원), aquarium (아쿠아리움), karaoke (노래방), bike ride (자전거 타기), bowling (볼링), flea market (벼룩시장), brunch (브런치), hike (등산, 하이킹), stayed (머물렀다), slept (잤다), visited (방문했다), played ((경기를) 했다).
Go through about six, new ones first, one word per turn: call highlight_word with the word, say it, and wait for the learner to say it before the next word. Never give several words in one turn. Now and then ask a tiny real question with the word (for example: Are you a morning person?) and react to the answer. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a word list.

Word list on screen: went (갔다) — "I went bowling."; met (만났다) — "I met Chloe."; saw (봤다) — "We saw fish."; ate (먹었다) — "We ate brunch."; bought (샀다) — "I bought a hat."; watched (봤다) — "I watched a movie."; cleaned (청소했다) — "I cleaned my room."; relaxed (쉬었다) — "I relaxed at home."; weekend (주말) — "last weekend"; among (~ 사이에서) — "popular among friends".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): questions about the learner's own life.

items: What did you do last weekend?
Did you have a good weekend?
Yes, I did. / It was okay.

steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "What did you do last weekend?" (hint on screen: I ___. It was ___.)
- "Did you have a good weekend?" (hint on screen: Yes, I did. / It was okay.)
- "Did you meet your friends?" (hint on screen: Yes, I met ___. / No, I didn’t.)
- "What did you eat on Sunday?" (hint on screen: I ate ___.)
- "Ask me about my weekend." (hint on screen: What did you do? / How about you?)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.

steps.title: Maya’s Bowling Day
steps.text: Last Saturday, Maya went bowling with her coworkers. She was *sort of* bad at it. *In addition to* bowling, they had pizza and played a game. After two hours, Maya was happy to *sit down*. On Sunday, she didn’t *get out* of bed until noon. *Although* her team lost, she had a great weekend.
steps.gloss: sort of 좀, 약간 · in addition to ~에 더해 · sit down 앉다 · get out of bed 침대에서 나오다 · until noon 낮 12시까지 · although ~이지만 · lost 졌다
questions: What did Maya do on Saturday?
When did she get out of bed on Sunday?
steps.teach:
Reading on screen: "Maya’s Bowling Day". Text: "Last Saturday, Maya went bowling with her coworkers. She was sort of bad at it. In addition to bowling, they had pizza and played a game. After two hours, Maya was happy to sit down. On Sunday, she didn’t get out of bed until noon. Although her team lost, she had a great weekend." Words: sort of 좀, 약간 · in addition to ~에 더해 · sit down 앉다 · get out of bed 침대에서 나오다 · until noon 낮 12시까지 · although ~이지만 · lost 졌다.
Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "What did Maya do on Saturday?" / "When did she get out of bed on Sunday?". React to their answers; if one is not right, point to the sentence. You may add one short personal question linked to the reading. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the 'I can' check-out.

steps.scene_desc: 금요일 저녁, 아파트 5층 복도. 큰 캠핑 배낭을 멘 그레이스와 퇴근해 돌아온 지우가 인사
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "What are you going to do this weekend?" (주말 계획). Goal: 계획을 묻고 말하기. Today's scene: 금요일 저녁, 아파트 5층 복도. 큰 캠핑 배낭을 멘 그레이스와 퇴근해 돌아온 지우가 인사. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above).
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "What are you going to do this weekend?".

steps.en: What are you going to do this weekend?
steps.extra: 대답: I’m going to ___.
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "What are you going to do this weekend?" (이번 주말에 뭐 할 거예요?). When to use it: 앞으로의 계획을 물어요. Note: 대답: I’m going to ___.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "I’m going to ___.".

steps.extra: I’m going to go camping. · I’m going to sleep in.
steps.teach:
Expression 2 of 3: "I’m going to ___." (~할 거예요.). When to use it: 정해 둔 계획을 말해요. Note: I’m going to go camping. · I’m going to sleep in.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "Have a good weekend!".

steps.extra: 대답: You too!
steps.teach:
Expression 3 of 3: "Have a good weekend!" (주말 잘 보내요!). When to use it: 금요일에 헤어질 때 하는 인사예요. Note: 대답: You too!
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the app plays a short scene ("Weekend Plans · 금요일 저녁, 5층 복도에서") in the characters' own voices — tell them to just listen.

If they say only part of it, say that line once and let them try once more, then go on. After the last line, give one short warm comment on how they did, then call next_step.

frame: What are you going to do this weekend?
head: 계획
이렇게 말해요
rows: visit my parents 부모님 댁 가기

steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: What are you going to do this weekend? / I’m going to ___. Table (계획 → 이렇게 말해요):
- go camping 캠핑 가기 → I’m going to go camping.
- visit my parents 부모님 댁 가기 → I’m going to visit my parents.
- sleep in 늦잠 자기 → I’m going to sleep in.
- nothing 아무것도 안 하기 → I’m not going to do anything.
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
정해 둔 계획: I’m *going to* visit my parents.
She’s *going to* sleep in a tent.
안 할 때: I’m *not* going to do anything.

미리 정한 계획은 *going to*.
*will*은 지금 결정한 일이나 앞으로의 일을 말할 때도 써요.
Maybe *I’ll* go hiking. 아마 등산 갈 거예요. (‘아마’는 Maybe)
errors: I’m going to visiting my parents.
I’m going to visit my parents.
What you are going to do?
What are you going to do?
I’m going to go to camping.
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- be going to + 동사: 정해 둔 계획: I’m going to visit my parents. / She’s going to sleep in a tent. / 안 할 때: I’m not going to do anything.
- going to · will: 미리 정한 계획은 going to. / will은 지금 결정한 일이나 앞으로의 일을 말할 때도 써요. / Maybe I’ll go hiking. 아마 등산 갈 거예요. (‘아마’는 Maybe)
Common mistakes on screen:
- I going to sleep in. → I’m going to sleep in. (am(’m)을 빼지 않아요.)
- I’m going to visiting my parents. → I’m going to visit my parents. (going to 뒤에는 동사 그대로.)
- What you are going to do? → What are you going to do? (물을 땐 are를 you 앞에.)
- I’m going to go to camping. → I’m going to go camping. (go camping·go hiking엔 to가 없어요.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. After that, go over each remaining mistake on screen in one short sentence (the wrong one, the right one and why), so that no mistake on screen is skipped. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.

Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) go hiking / Saturday → I’m going to go hiking on Saturday. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: go hiking → Saturday | visit a museum → Sunday | have a barbecue → tonight | see a concert → Friday.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to their answer, praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

cards: What are you going to do this weekend?
steps.teach:
This is the start of session 2 of "What are you going to do this weekend?" (주말 계획); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say. Start the review only after the learner has answered at least two of your small-talk questions.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "What are you going to do this weekend?" / "I’m going to ___." / "Have a good weekend!". One at a time: give a tiny real situation, wait for their answer and react naturally, then the next. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

groups: I’m going to visit my parents.
I’m not going to do anything.
steps.teach:
More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 계획 말하기: "I’m going to visit my parents." (부모님 댁에 갈 거예요., 보통); "I’m going to sleep in." (늦잠 잘 거예요., 친근); "I’m not going to do anything." (아무것도 안 할 거예요., 보통); "Maybe I’ll go hiking." (아마 등산 갈 거예요., 보통)

- 대답·인사: "Nothing special." (별일 없어요., 보통); "Sounds fun!" (재미있겠다!, 친근); "You too!" (당신도요!, 친근); "Let me know." (알려 줘요., 친근)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life and take them one per turn: say one, wait for the learner to say it and react, then the next. Then use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.

items: I’m not going to do anything.
steps.teach:
Word list on screen: nothing (아무것도 ~ 않음) — "Nothing special."; anything (무엇이든, 아무것도) — "I’m not going to do anything."; pub (술집(영국식)) — "a quiet pub"; plan (계획) — "Any plans?"; going (~할 예정인) — "I’m going to rest."; visit (방문하다) — "visit my parents"; special (특별한) — "nothing special"; maybe (아마) — "Maybe I’ll go."; know (알다) — "Let me know."; suppose (~라고 생각하다) — "I suppose so.".

steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "What are you going to do this weekend?" (hint on screen: I’m going to ___. (예: I’m going to visit my parents.))
- "Any plans for Saturday night?" (hint on screen: Nothing special. / I’m going to ___.)
- "Are you going to sleep in on Sunday?" (hint on screen: Yes, I am. / No, I’m not.)
- "What are you going to do on your next holiday?" (hint on screen: I’m going to ___. / Maybe I’ll ___.)
- "It’s Friday. Say goodbye to me." (hint on screen: Have a good weekend! — You too!)

Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.

steps.title: Grace’s Camping Trip
steps.text: Grace is going to go camping this weekend with two friends. They’re going to *set up* a tent near a lake. There is nothing *in particular* to do there. They’re just going to grill food and look at the stars. Last time, they *ended up* sleeping in the car because of the rain! This time, Grace is going to check the weather first.
steps.gloss: set up 치다, 세우다 · lake 호수 · in particular 특별히 · grill 굽다 · stars 별 · end up 결국 ~하게 되다

Reading on screen: "Grace’s Camping Trip". Text: "Grace is going to go camping this weekend with two friends. They’re going to set up a tent near a lake. There is nothing in particular to do there. Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "Where are they going to set up the tent?" / "Where did they sleep last time?". React to their answers; if one is not right, point to the sentence. You may add one short personal question linked to the reading. Then call next_step.

steps.title: 좋아하는 계절
steps.scene_desc: 가을 오후, 동네 공원 벤치. 노랗고 빨간 단풍 아래 대니얼과 지우가 커피를 들고 앉아 있고, 하늘은 맑고 파람
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "What’s your favorite season?" (좋아하는 계절). Goal: 좋아하는 것을 말하고 이유 대기. Today's scene: 가을 오후, 동네 공원 벤치. 노랗고 빨간 단풍 아래 대니얼과 지우가 커피를 들고 앉아 있고, 하늘은 맑고 파람. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in one or two short sentences what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene, and in a few words where the scene happens and who meets (from Today's scene above).
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "What’s your favorite season?".

steps.extra: 대답: My favorite season is fall.
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "What’s your favorite season?" (제일 좋아하는 계절이 뭐예요?). When to use it: 좋아하는 계절을 물어요. Note: 대답: My favorite season is fall.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "My favorite season is ___.".

steps.extra: My favorite season is spring.
steps.teach:
Expression 2 of 3: "My favorite season is ___." (제일 좋아하는 계절은 ~예요.). When to use it: 좋아하는 계절을 말해요. Note: My favorite season is spring.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "Because it’s ___.".

steps.title: Fall Leaves · 가을 오후, 공원에서

lines.en: Look at the leaves, Jiwoo. They’re beautiful.
I know. Fall is the best!
Really? {{What’s your favorite season}}?
{{My favorite season is}} fall.
Why?
{{Because it’s}} cool, and the sky is so blue.

lines.en: Summer is too hot for me.
Ha! What about winter?

steps.teach:
The app has just played this scene, "Fall Leaves · 가을 오후, 공원에서", in the characters' own voices. The learner heard it and sees it on screen:
1. Daniel: "Look at the leaves, Jiwoo. They’re beautiful." (나뭇잎 좀 봐요, 지우. 예쁘네요.)
2. Jiwoo: "I know. Fall is the best!" (그러게요. 가을이 최고예요!)
3. Daniel: "Really? What’s your favorite season?" (그래요? 제일 좋아하는 계절이 뭐예요?)
4. Jiwoo: "My favorite season is fall." (제일 좋아하는 계절은 가을이에요.)
5. Daniel: "Why?" (왜요?)
6. Jiwoo: "Because it’s cool, and the sky is so blue." (시원하고, 하늘이 정말 파라니까요.)
7. Daniel: "Me? I love summer. I go to the sea every year." (저요? 저는 여름이 좋아요. 해마다 바다에 가요.)
8. Jiwoo: "Summer is too hot for me." (여름은 저한테 너무 더워요.)
9. Daniel: "Ha! What about winter?" (하하! 겨울은요?)
10. Jiwoo: "I don’t like winter. It’s too cold. But I like it when it snows." (겨울은 싫어요. 너무 추워요. 그래도 눈 올 때는 좋아요.)
11. Daniel: "Me, too! Snow covers the trees. It’s so pretty." (저도요! 눈이 나무를 덮잖아요. 정말 예뻐요.)
12. Jiwoo: "Then we both like winter a little!" (그럼 우리 둘 다 겨울을 조금은 좋아하네요!)
Talk about it like a person: a short natural reaction, then one simple question about what happened (the answer is in the lines above). React to their answer; if it is not right, point kindly to the line that shows it. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): role reading of that scene.

Then go in order, one line at a time: call highlight_line with the line number before each line, read your line, and for the learner's line just wait for them to say it. If they say only part of it, say that line once and let them try once more, then go on. After the last line, give one short warm comment on how they did, then call next_step.

Before you judge an answer, check the scene lines carefully: who said what. Ask one statement at a time: read it yourself and ask True or false?. Accept true/false, yes/no, or Korean (맞아요/아니에요). Say whether they are right and point to the line that shows it in a few words, also when they are right. In Korean say the answer as 정답은 True예요 / 정답은 False예요. There are 3 statements: ask every one and wait for an answer to each (Oh or Hmm is not an answer). Only after you have checked the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a table of useful sentences for real situations.

frame: My favorite season is ___. Because it’s ___.
head: 계절
이유
이렇게 말해요
rows: I love spring because of the flowers.
I love summer because of the sea.
Fall is the best because it’s cool.
I like winter because it snows.
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: What’s your favorite season? / My favorite season is ___. Because it’s ___. Table (계절 → 이유):
- spring 봄 → flowers
- summer 여름 → the sea
- fall 가을 → cool
- winter 겨울 → snow
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
이유를 말할 땐 *because* + 문장.
I like fall *because* it’s cool.
물으면 짧게: Why? — *Because* it’s cool.

낱말(명사)만 올 땐 *because of*.
I love spring *because of* the flowers.
because 뒤에는 문장, because of 뒤에는 낱말
errors: I like spring because the flowers.
I like spring because of the flowers.
My favorite season is a fall.
계절 이름 앞에 a를 넣지 않아요.
Summer is too hot to me.
Summer is too hot for me.
I like fall because it’s cool.
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- because + 문장: 이유를 말할 땐 because + 문장. / I like fall because it’s cool. / 물으면 짧게: Why? — Because it’s cool.
- because of + 낱말: 낱말(명사)만 올 땐 because of. / I love spring because of the flowers. / because 뒤에는 문장, because of 뒤에는 낱말
Common mistakes on screen:
- I like spring because the flowers. → I like spring because of the flowers. (낱말만 오면 because of.)
- My favorite season is a fall. → My favorite season is fall. (계절 이름 앞에 a를 넣지 않아요.)
- Summer is too hot to me. → Summer is too hot for me. (‘나한테는’은 for me.)
- I like fall because cool. → I like fall because it’s cool. (because 뒤에는 문장(it’s cool).)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. After that, go over each remaining mistake on screen in one short sentence (the wrong one, the right one and why), so that no mistake on screen is skipped. Keep it light, then call next_step.

steps.note: 예) spring / warm → My favorite season is spring because it’s warm. · the sea → because of the sea
steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) spring / warm → My favorite season is spring because it’s warm. · the sea → because of the sea. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: spring → warm | summer → the sea | fall → the leaves | winter → snow.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and stop there to wait for their answer. In your next reply, react to their answer, praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

This is the start of session 2 of "What’s your favorite season?" (좋아하는 계절); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say. Start the review only after the learner has answered at least two of your small-talk questions.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "What’s your favorite season?" / "My favorite season is ___." / "Because it’s ___.". One at a time: give a tiny real situation, wait for their answer and react naturally, then the next. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

groups: I love spring because of the flowers.
I like it when it snows.
Summer is too hot for me.
steps.teach:
More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 좋아하는 계절: "I love spring because of the flowers." (꽃 때문에 봄이 정말 좋아요., 보통); "Fall is the best." (가을이 최고예요., 친근); "The leaves are beautiful." (단풍이 예뻐요., 보통); "I like it when it snows." (눈 올 때가 좋아요., 보통)
- 싫은 계절: "I don’t like winter." (겨울은 싫어요., 보통); "It’s too cold." (너무 추워요., 보통); "Summer is too hot for me." (여름은 저한테 너무 더워요., 보통)
- 맞장구: "What about you?" (당신은요?, 보통); "Me, too!" (저도요!, 친근)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life and take them one per turn: say one, wait for the learner to say it and react, then the next. Then use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.
